## NCT07618559
The Food Network Effect: A Study of Food Related Visual Stimuli and Postoperative Gastrointestinal Recovery

Intervention: : Food Related Visual Stimuli Exposure — This intervention consists of a structured, non-pharmacologic behavioral exposure to food related visual stimuli delivered during predefined peri-meal periods throughout the postoperative hospitalization. Participants will view food centered television programming (e.g., cooking, baking, or food preparation shows) for a minimum of 15 minutes during each designated meal window: breakfast (7:00-9:00 AM), lunch (12:00-2:00 PM), and dinner (5:00-7:00 PM).

Unlike standard television viewing or unrestricted media use, the intervention uses scheduled exposure to food-specific visual content intended to provide cephalic phase sensory stimulation during times corresponding with routine eating periods. The intervention is delivered using existing hospital television resources and does not involve medications, dietary modification, invasive procedures, or additional medical devices. Adherence will be assessed through participant self-report and periodic study team monitoring.

## NCT07673575
EFFECT OF MULLIGAN CERVICAL SUSTAINED NATURAL APOPHYSEAL GLIDE ON POSTURAL STABILITY IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC NECK PAIN

Intervention: : 1- The Biodex Balance System (BBS) — The Biodex Balance System SD Model 950-441(Biodex Medical Systems, Inc.) is a multi-dimensional (static and dynamic) postural control assessment and training system. It provides objective, valid, and reliable measures of a patient's ability to balance on stable and unstable surfaces. It measures the overall Stability Index (OSI), anterior/posterior stability index (APSI), and medial/lateral stability index (MLSI). Its intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) reliability is R = 0.92 (OSI), R = 0.89 (APSI), and R = 0.93 (MLSI). Chronic neck pain subjects have demonstrated significantly worse Biodex balance performance across OSI, APSI, and MLSI
: 2-The Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) — The Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) is a unidimensional measure of pain intensity that serves as a segmented numerical version of the visual analog scale (VAS). It consists of an 11-point scale where the respondent selects a whole number from 0 to 10 that best reflects the intensity of their pain, with 0 representing "no pain" and 10 representing the "worst imaginable pain" .

The NPRS has demonstrated high construct and criterion validity for assessing pain severity in patients with chronic musculoskeletal disorders. It is considered a valid tool for differentiating pain characteristics between individuals with chronic neck pain and healthy controls. The research suggests that the NPRS is often more responsive to clinical changes and easier for patients to comprehend than the traditional VAS .This scale is characterized by excellent test-retest reliability (ICC: 0.95),
: 3- The Neck Disability Index (Arabic version) for functional disability — Neck disability index (NDI) is self-reported assessment includes ten items: pain severity, personal care, lifting, work, headaches, concentration, sleeping, driving, reading, and recreation. Higher scores imply a greater level of disability. Arabic version of the NDI was used to assess Arabic patients with neck pain, as the Arabic version of the NDI is reliable and valid
: 4- Digital Inclinometer for Cervical Range of Motion — A digital inclinometer is a handheld electronic device used to objectively measure the degrees of spinal curvature by detecting inclination relative to the force of gravity.In cervical spine assessment, it is used to quantify movements including flexion, extension, lateral flexion, and rotation.The digital inclinometer is recognized as a highly valid and reliable instrument for measuring cervical range of motion (CROM). Recent studies have reported excellent intra-rater and inter-rater reliability (ICC \> 0.85), particularly for cervical rotation and lateral flexion. It is often preferred over traditional goniometry because it provides precise, objective, and quantitative data that is less susceptible to manual measurement error.
: 5- Arabic Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia (TSK-11) — The TSK-11 is a shortened, 11-item version of the original Tampa Scale, designed to assess kinesiophobia. Defined as an irrational and debilitating fear of physical movement resulting from a feeling of vulnerability to painful injury or re-injury . The Arabic version was developed to provide a linguistically and culturally adapted tool for assessing fear-avoidance beliefs in Arabic-speaking populations. The Arabic version of the TSK-11 has been cross- culturally validated and demonstrates strong psychometric properties. It exhibits high internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha values typically ranging from 0.86 to 0.90, and excellent test-retest reliability. It shows significant concurrent validity, as scores are strongly correlated with pain intensity (NPRS) and functional disability measures like the Neck Disability Index.
: 6- Overhead LASER pointer for Cervical proprioception — An overhead LASER pointer will be used to assess cervical proprioception by performing the Cervical Joint Position Error (JPE) test. The Joint Position Sense Error (JPSE) is considered one of the essential measures to clinically assess cervical proprioception. The test has good (ICC: 0.77-0.78)
: Mulligan Cervical SNAG Technique Protocol — Patient positioning: Seated or standing, with spine in neutral or slight flexion.

* Therapist hand placement: Thumb or fingers on the targeted cervical vertebra (e.g., C2-C7 or upper thoracic T1-T4).
* Direction of glide: Anterior and upward glide along the plane of the facet joint, synchronized with the patient's active movement (e.g., rotation, extension)
* Repetitions: 10 repetitions per session, each held for 10 seconds, with rest intervals.
* Session structure: SNAG mobilizations performed first, followed by conventional exercises.
* Cervical spine: Targeted for joint position sense, pain, and dizziness.

Technique variations:

• Minor adjustments in force direction to optimize symptom reduction.
: Conventional therapy group — Based on the American Physical Therapy Association (APTA) Clinical Practice Guidelines for Neck Pain with Mobility Deficits, participants in the conventional therapy group received a multimodal treatment program consisting of mobility exercises, strengthening and endurance training, stretching exercises, and patient education

* Cervical and thoracic mobility exercises.
* Strengthening and endurance exercises for the deep cervical flexors, cervical extensors, and scapulothoracic muscles.
* Stretching exercises for the upper trapezius, levator scapulae, pectoral, and cervical muscles.
* Patient education regarding posture, ergonomics, activity modification, and self-management strategies.

Sequencing:

• SNAG mobilizations performed at session start, followed by active exercises and stretching

Manual therapy timing:

• SNAG component adds \~10 minutes to a 20-minute exercise session
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07673575

Treatment at the target dose is then continued for 14 days. From cycle 2 onward, sonrotoclax is generally administered on days 1-14 of each 28-day cycle. Dose interruptions, reductions, and adjustments to treatment duration or concomitant medications follow the protocol.
: Azacitidine (AZA) — Azacitidine is administered at 75 mg/m² once daily by subcutaneous injection or intravenous infusion for seven consecutive days per 28-day cycle. In cycle 1, azacitidine is administered on days 4-10, beginning when sonrotoclax reaches its target dose. From cycle 2 onward, azacitidine is administered on days 1-7. Treatment delays and dose modifications are permitted according to protocol-defined toxicity and recovery criteria.

Effectiveness of Buzzy Bee Device in Anxiety Reduction and Pain Control During Local Anesthesia Administration

Intervention: : Intervention A: Buzzy® Bee-Assisted Local Anesthesia — Behavioral Guidance: Child preparation using the Tell-Show-Do technique.

Device Application: The Buzzy® Bee device (equipped with pre-frozen wings) is activated to provide combined high-frequency vibration and cryotherapy. It is placed on the extraoral cheek skin approximately 1-2 cm proximal to the target injection site for 30 seconds prior to needle insertion and remains continuously active throughout needle insertion and solution deposition.

Topical Anesthesia: Injection site is isolated with cotton rolls, dried, and treated with 2% Lidocaine gel applied for 2 minutes via a sterile cotton swab.

: Intervention B: Conventional Local Anesthesia Technique — Behavioral Guidance: Child preparation using standard Tell-Show-Do behavioral guidance paired with routine audiovisual distraction (cartoons displayed on a chair-side screen).

Topical Anesthesia: Identical protocol to Intervention A (site isolation, drying, and 2% Lidocaine gel application for 2 minutes).

Local Anesthesia Injection: Maxillary buccal infiltration delivered using 4% Articaine with 1:200,000 epinephrine via a sterile short 27-gauge needle, deposited slowly over 60 seconds using identical technique, volume, and rate as Intervention A, but without external vibration or cryotherapy application.

## NCT07887698
Effects of Instrument-Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization Versus Post Facilitation Stretch Technique in Chronic Neck Pain

Intervention: : Instrument Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization — Instrument-Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization (IASTM) is a manual therapy technique that utilizes specially designed stainless-steel instruments to detect and treat soft tissue restrictions, myofascial adhesions, and scar tissue. The technique involves applying controlled mechanical pressure using longitudinal, fanning, and cross-fiber strokes to improve tissue mobility, enhance local circulation, stimulate tissue remodeling, and reduce pain. In this study, IASTM will be applied to the upper trapezius, levator scapulae, and suboccipital muscles following conventional physiotherapy. The intervention aims to restore normal soft tissue mobility, improve cervical range of motion, decrease pain, and enhance functional outcomes in individuals with chronic neck pain.
: Post Facilitation Stretch — Post Facilitation Stretch (PFS) is a muscle energy-based manual therapy technique designed to reduce muscle tightness, improve flexibility, and restore normal muscle length through neuromuscular inhibition. The technique involves positioning the target muscle at its initial barrier, followed by a controlled submaximal isometric contraction against therapist resistance for 5-10 seconds. After the contraction, the patient relaxes while the therapist gently stretches the muscle to a new barrier. This sequence is repeated for 3-5 cycles to enhance muscle extensibility and reduce stiffness. In this study, PFS will be applied to the upper trapezius, levator scapulae, and suboccipital muscles following conventional physiotherapy to improve cervical mobility, reduce pain, and enhance functional outcomes in individuals with chronic neck pain.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07887698

SUMMARY:

## NCT06777212
Mindfulness Intervention and Its Impact on Psychological and Family Dynamics in Children With Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors.

Intervention: : Mindfulness Training Program — The Mindfulness Training Program is a 30-day behavioral intervention designed to help children with body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs) such as nail-biting, skin-picking, and hair-pulling. Delivered through JD Health, the program includes daily audio-guided exercises focused on mindfulness techniques such as deep breathing, body scans, and emotional awareness. Children will be encouraged to practice mindfulness for 10-15 minutes each day, with the goal of improving emotional regulation, reducing impulsive behavior, and enhancing self-awareness. Family support is involved, with parents helping children track their progress and offering reinforcement.
: Psychosocial Education Program — The Psychosocial Education Program is a 30-day behavioral intervention designed for children with body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs), including nail-biting, skin-picking, and hair-pulling. Delivered through JD Health, the program provides daily educational content in the form of articles and coping strategies. The intervention focuses on improving emotional regulation, promoting family support, and developing positive behavioral strategies. Parents play an active role by reviewing the content with their children and helping them apply the strategies in daily life. Behavioral and psychological assessments are conducted at baseline, one month, and three months to evaluate the program's impact.

It involves placing a cap with small sensors on the child's head to measure the brain's electrical activity. This technique does not send any energy into the brain. The investigators will use the HD-EEG to measure motor-evoked potentials (MEPs) and TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs).

## NCT07637539
Proactive Liver Disease Assessment and Brief Intervention Among Hospitalized People With Harmful Alcohol Consumption: An Investigator-initiated, Pragmatic, Parallel-group, Open-label, 2-arm Randomized Controlled Trial to Investigate the Efficacy of Proactive Elastography-based Brief Alcohol Intervention Compared With Usual Care in Hospitalized Adult Participants at Risk of Alcohol-related Liver Disease

Intervention: : Elastography-based brief alcohol intervention — Participants randomized to elastography-based BAI will receive elastography assessment during first hospitalization. Elastography is a widely validated ultrasound-based technique that measures liver stiffness as a surrogate marker of liver fibrosis. The BAI will be delivered according to the FRAMES model, a structured, evidence-based framework for brief motivational interventions targeting harmful alcohol use. The intervention is patient-centered, non-confrontational, and based on principles of motivational interviewing. Both the elastography and the BAI will last approximately 10-15 minutes and will be delivered by trained study personnel directly following elastography assessment. At 3 months, participants will receive BAI by telephone. Follow-up reinforcement of elastography-based BAI will subsequently be provided during scheduled visits at 6 and 12 months.

Each session will consist of 2,000 shock waves delivered at a frequency of 6-8 hertz (Hz) and a pressure of 1.8-2.5 bar. The ESWT probe will be placed directly on the skin over the predetermined bone marrow edema (BME) area identified by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
: Sham Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy — Sham radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) will be administered once weekly for 5 consecutive weeks using the same BTL-6000 SWT TOPLINE device. The device will be operated at a low setting to reproduce the characteristic treatment sound without delivering therapeutically effective shock waves. The ESWT probe will be held close to the skin over the predetermined bone marrow edema (BME) area identified by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), without direct contact. Simultaneously, an inactive ultrasound probe similar in size to the ESWT probe will be placed directly on the skin over the treatment area to reproduce the physical sensation of active treatment.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07887893

SUMMARY:

Intervention: : Self-Managed Contraceptive Care — This intervention is designed to expand access to self-managed family planning methods among women and girls in settings with weak last-mile service delivery. Contraceptive self-care - encompassing self-administered injectable contraception, oral contraceptive pills, emergency contraception, and other user-controlled methods - offers a complementary model of service delivery that can bypass structural barriers by placing tools and decision-making directly in the hands of users. Self-care approaches are particularly important for women experiencing intimate partner violence or reproductive coercion, for whom discrete and self-managed contraception may be the only accessible option.

Intervention mechanisms will include a network of trained self-care promoters; targeted information, education, and communication (IEC) materials, direct commodity provision; facility provider training on self-care counseling; and client decision-support tools.

## NCT07888634
Effects of Remote Ischemic Preconditioning at Different Time Phases on Clinical Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Heart Valve Surgery

Intervention: : remote ischemic preconditioning — The patient lies in the supine position, exposes the upper limbs, uses a sphygmomanometer, and ties the cuff to the upper limbs with a tightness that can accommodate one finger. The distance between the lower edge of the cuff and the antecubital space is 2cm. First, measure the patient's basal blood pressure. If the systolic blood pressure is less than 180mmHg, proceed to the next step of RIPC. In the same way, tie the compression therapy device cuff to the patient's upper limb, quickly pressurize to the pressure value of "basal systolic blood pressure + 50mmHg", maintain it for 5 minutes, and then quickly decompress to 0mmHg and maintain it for 5 minutes. This is an upper limb ischemia-reperfusion cycle. The ischemia-reperfusion procedure was repeated three times in total. The maximum pressure value during the operation shall not exceed 200mmHg. If the patient's systolic blood pressure is higher than 180mmHg or the hemodynamics is unstable, the intervention will be stopped.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07888634

## NCT07889128
Holistic Approaches for Organizational Well-being of Healthcare Professionals: a Randomized Clinical Trial Protocol

Intervention: : Caring Massage — Caring Massage® is a nursing intervention based on intentional, mindful touch and an empathetic caring relationship. A certified nurse will perform the intervention on predefined body areas, including the face, back, shoulders, arms, hands, legs, and feet, according to a standardized protocol. Oil or moisturizing cream will be used to facilitate the massage. Sessions will take place in a dedicated setting that ensures privacy and comfort, after the participant's work shift. Participants will receive eight sessions over one month, twice weekly, lasting up to 30 minutes each, with at least 48 hours between sessions.
: Serenity Room — The Serenity room intervention provides controlled multisensory stimulation inspired by Snoezelen principles. The environment includes soft lighting with gradual color changes, ceiling-mounted fiber optics, background music, reduced external noise, and ergonomic seating. Each 30-minute session includes 10 minutes of acclimatization, 10 minutes of seated relaxation, and 10 minutes of gradual reorientation. Trained Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technicians will supervise the sessions and adjust light and sound intensity to individual preferences. Participants will attend eight sessions over one month, twice weekly, after their work shift, with at least 48 hours between sessions.
: Combined Serenity Room and Caring Massage — The Combined Caring and Multisensory intervention alternates Caring Massage® with Serenity room sessions. Caring Massage® involves intentional, mindful touch delivered by a certified nurse according to a standardized protocol. Serenity room sessions provide controlled multisensory stimulation through soft lighting, background music, and comfortable seating, supervised by trained Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technicians. Participants will attend two sessions per week after their work shift for one month, for a total of eight sessions: four Caring Massage® sessions and four Serenity room sessions. Each session will last up to 30 minutes, with at least 48 hours between sessions.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07889128

## NCT07889375
An Open-label, Multicenter, Randomized, Parallel-group Trial to Assess Glycemic Control With the RIGHTEST iFree 2 Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in Adults With Diabetes Mellitus

Intervention: : Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) — Participants assigned to this arm will use a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system as the main tool for day-to-day glucose management. The system consists of a disposable subcutaneous glucose sensor, a reusable transmitter, and the RIGHTEST iFree 2 smartphone application for real-time data display and alerts. Sensors are worn continuously and replaced according to the product labeling over the \~6-month study period. CGM data will be reviewed by participants and study clinicians to guide self-management and diabetes treatment adjustments in addition to usual care.
: Self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) — Participants assigned to this arm will use self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) with a capillary finger-stick blood glucose meter as their primary tool for day-to-day diabetes management. An approved meter (e.g., RIGHTEST Max Plus blood glucose meter) and test strips will be provided, together with training on correct use and recording of results. Participants will measure their blood glucose at a frequency consistent with routine diabetes care and the recommendations of their treating physician (for example before meals, at bedtime, and as clinically indicated). SMBG values and downloaded meter records will be reviewed at study visits to guide insulin and other diabetes treatment adjustments. No real-time continuous glucose monitoring data will be used in this arm.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07889375

## NCT07890337
Rehabilitation Through Virtual Immersion & Integrated Exposure for Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (ReVIVE for mTBI)

Intervention: : Virtual Reality — ReVIVE is a virtual reality (VR)-based rehabilitation intervention delivered over six weekly sessions as an adjunct to standard care for individuals with PTSD following mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Using an Oculus Quest VR headset, participants complete approximately 10 minutes of acclimation followed by 30 minutes of immersive activities. The intervention incorporates mindfulness, breathing and grounding exercises, emotional regulation, and cognitive and functional activities within simulated everyday environments. Scenarios are designed to support engagement with progressively more complex environments and tasks. Intervention tolerability is monitored using the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire before and after VR sessions. Standard care, including routine psychotherapy and medication management, continues throughout the study.
: Standard Psychotherapy — Standard psychotherapy consists of ongoing therapy received by participants before enrollment and continued throughout the study as part of the participants usual care. Sessions focus on identifying emotions, recognizing cognitive shifts and difficulties, supporting real-time emotional and cognitive regulation, and facilitating interpersonal processing and emotional labeling. Psychotherapy frequency and treatment decisions remain at the discretion of participants' treating clinicians and are not standardized or altered by the study. Participants assigned to the control arm continue standard psychotherapy and medication management without receiving the study's virtual reality intervention.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07890337

## NCT07890389
Dynamic Versus Static Jaw Relation for Implant Supported Prosthesis: Crossover Study of Chewing Efficiency

Intervention: : Conventional Static Jaw Relation Registration — Conventional static maxillomandibular relationship registration for the fabrication of an implant-supported full-arch zirconia prosthesis. Maxillary and mandibular record bases and occlusion rims will be used to record the vertical dimension of occlusion and centric relation. A facebow transfer and semi-adjustable articulator will be used for maxillary cast mounting and articulator adjustment. Chewing efficiency will be evaluated using a two-color chewing gum mixing test at the prespecified assessment time points.
: Dynamic Digital Jaw Tracking Registration — Dynamic digital maxillomandibular relationship registration for the fabrication of an implant-supported full-arch zirconia prosthesis. Digital impressions of the maxillary and mandibular arches will be obtained using an intraoral scanner. A digital jaw tracking device and a central bearing device attached to the record bases will be used to record mandibular movements and dynamic jaw relations. Intervention: : Electromyographic Biofeedback (EMG-BF) — Electromyographic biofeedback (EMG-BF) will be applied using a Neurotrack Myplus Pro 4 device and surface electrodes. Participants will be positioned in the left lateral position. Surface electrodes will be placed around the anus at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions and on the transversus abdominis muscle. A ground electrode will be placed on the arm. Participants will practice pelvic floor and anal sphincter contraction and relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, and abdominal muscle contraction while maintaining pelvic floor and anal sphincter relaxation. The training will aim to improve coordination among the abdominal muscles, respiratory muscles, pelvic floor, and anal sphincter. Each session will last approximately 20-25 minutes. EMG-BF will be provided twice weekly for 6 weeks, for a total of 12 sessions.
: Connective Tissue Massage (CTM) — Connective tissue massage (CTM) will be applied to the lumbosacral region, progressing toward the thoracic, scapular, interscapular, and cervico-occipital regions. Before treatment, connective tissue mobility and circulatory responses will be assessed by palpation. Participants will sit upright with their hips, knees, and ankles flexed at 90 degrees. Tissue mobilization will be performed using the palmar surface of the third finger, with the distal interphalangeal joint flexed at 45-60 degrees. Each stroke will be repeated three times. Sessions will last approximately 5-15 minutes, depending on the treated region. CTM will be provided twice weekly for 6 weeks, for a total of 12 sessions, in addition to EMG-BF and patient education.

* The intervention involves several key technical steps designed to preserve gastric function and prevent postoperative reflux:

Surgical Approach and Resection: The procedure begins with a laparoscopic or robotic proximal gastrectomy accompanied by D1+ lymph node dissection

* Surgeons must preserve the hepatic branch of the vagus nerve in all patients
* The esophagus is resected just above the esophagogastric junction (EGJ) using a linear stapler

Anchoring and Fixation: To create an anti-reflux mechanism, the proximal part of the residual stomach and the distal esophagus (3 cm above the transected edge) are fixed using single interrupted sutures on both sides

## NCT07251010
Phrenoesophageal Ligament Reconstruction With Mesh: A New Approach to Hiatal Hernia Repair (Alinasser's Technique) for Adult Patients With Symptomatic Hiatus Hernia: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Phrenoesophageal Ligament Reconstruction with Mesh: A New Approach to Hiatal Hernia Repair (Alinasser's Technique) — Alinasser's technique of laparoscopic hiatal hernia repair (LHHR) is carried out, follow same steps of classical approach except before closing the crura A non-absorbable mesh (≈2.0 x 10.0 cm) is sutured to the esophagus( lower mediastinal esophagus) , just above the hiatus by four 2-0 prolene stitches. The continuity of the mesh is then fixed just below the hiatus anteriorly on the abdominal face of diaphragm by four 2-0 prolene stitches. About half of the mesh is fixed to the esophagus and the other half is fixed to the diaphragm. If there is no space for mesh fixation on the diaphragm, the left hepatic triangular ligament will be released.
: Classic approach — Classic approach of laparoscopic hiatal hernia repair (LHHR) is performed under general anesthesia with the patient in the French position and pneumoperitoneum established at 15 mmHg CO₂. Port placement follows a standardized foregut approach, with a camera port in the epigastrium and additional working ports placed under direct vision. After retracting the left lobe of the liver, the diaphragmatic hiatus is exposed. The stomach and hernia sac are reduced by dividing short gastric vessels and mobilizing the gastric fundus to free the left crus. Circumferential dissection of the hernia sac continues cranially to gain at least 3-5 cm of intraabdominal esophageal length.The diaphragmatic crura are approximated posterior to the esophagus, aided by a calibration tube. If necessary. A posterior 270° Toupét fundoplication is then constructed with interrupted stitches, anchoring the wrap to the esophagus and crura.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07251010

## NCT07454707
Randomized Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Very Low Dose Anticoagulant Therapy Added to Standard-Care Single Antiplatelet Therapy for Prevention of Recurrent Strokes in Patients With Ischemic Stroke Aged 75+ Years

Intervention: : Edoxaban 15 mg — Edoxaban is a once-daily oral tablet. It can be taken with or without food. Edoxaban is widely used worldwide for the prevention of stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation, treatment of venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT/PE. It works by inhibiting a coagulation protein called Factor Xa to reduce thrombin generation and prevent blood clots. For this trial, the dose of edoxaban chosen is 15 mg once a day (which is one-quarter of the full dose) to minimize the chance of bleeding problems. The 15 mg dose of edoxaban has been shown to be safe and effective for preventing strokes in patients with atrial fibrillation, but it has not yet been studied for stroke prevention in patients without atrial fibrillation.

## NCT07472868
MEND-IT II: Neoadjuvant FOLFOXIRI and Chemoradiotherapy Versus Neoadjuvant CAPOX/FOLFOX and Chemoradiotherapy, Followed by Surgery or a Watch-and-Wait Approach in High Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

Intervention: : FOLFOXIRI — ICT consists of four or six two-weekly cycles of FOLFOXIRI. The dosages, dosage modification, and methods and schedule of administration of FOLFOXIRI follows the established treatment protocols and standard of care as prescribed in the Dutch Guidelines. It is administered as follows:

* Day 1: irinotecan 165 mg/m2 body-surface area (BSA) intravenously (IV), followed by oxaliplatin 85mg/m2 BSA IV in combination with leucovorin 400mg/m2 BSA, followed by:
* Day 1-2: 3200 mg/m2 BSA of continuous 5-fluorouracil IV
* Day 3-14: rest days.
: CAPOX — The dosages, dosage modification, and methods and schedule of administration of CAPOX follows the established treatment protocols and standard of care as prescribed in the Dutch Guidelines. CAPOX is administered as follows:

* Day 1: Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 body-surface area \[BSA\], intravenously \[IV\].
* Day 1-14: Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 BSA, orally, twice daily.
* Day 15-21: Rest days.

This regimen is initially administered for three cycles. In case of responsive or stable disease, a 4th cycle of CAPOX will be administered. In case of unacceptable toxicity (physician's discretion) to oxaliplatin, CAPOX may be continued as FOLFOX.
: FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil, Leucovorin, Oxaliplatin) — FOLFOX is a combination chemotherapy regimen, consisting of:

* 5-fluorouracil (chemical name: L01BC02; trade name: 5-Fluorouracil; formulation: concentrate for solution for injection)
* Oxaliplatin (chemical name: L01XA03; trade name: Oxaliplatin Accord; formulation: concentrate for solution for injection)

FOLFOX is a well-established chemotherapy combination regimen for colorectal cancer, and is authorised for its intended use in this study. All FOLFOX component agents will be sourced from commercially available hospital stock and prepared according to standard protocols at participating centres.
: Chemoradiotherapy — In accordance with established standard-of-care protocols, chemoradiotherapy will commence 3-6 weeks after the completion of ICT, following restaging imaging and MDT review. The standard chemoradiotherapy regimen consists of external beam radiotherapy 50Gy in fractions of 2 Gy or 50.4 Gy in fractions of 1.8Gy combined with concomitant capecitabine, administered in accordance with Dutch Guidelines:

* Dosage: 825 mg/m² Body Surface Area (BSA), twice daily
* Route of administration: orally
* Schedule: administered on all radiotherapy days
* Treatment duration: 25 days

In the case of cardiotoxicity or severe hand-foot syndrome due to capecitabine, treatment may be switched to Teysuno, in accordance with the Dutch guideline. The recommended dose of Teysuno in combination with oxaliplatin is 25 mg/m² body surface area, administered twice daily.
: Total mesorectal excision (+/- IORT) — In patients with an incomplete response and resectable disease after first restaging, surgery is performed according to standard of care by a surgical oncologist with experience in rectal cancer surgery within 10-14 weeks after completion of chemoradiotherapy. The type and extent of the surgery is left to the discretion of the operating surgeon. In case of need for reconstructive surgery, the required specialist will be consulted and will attend the surgical procedure. The addition of IORT will be left to the discretion of the surgeon.
: Watch-and-wait approach — When a cCR is achieved after neoadjuvant therapy, patients may opt for a W\&W approach. A cCR is confirmed by imaging, endoscopy and digital rectal examination. Patients will receive a close surveillance follow up scheme according to the standard of care and local guidelines (51-54). Conduct follow-up every 3 months in the first year, every 6 months in the second year, and every 6 to 12 months in years 3 to 5, consisting of MRI and endoscopic evaluation. If any changes to the scar are detected during follow-up, a biopsy should be performed.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07472868

First-in-man Trial to Assess the Safety, Performance and Clinical Benefit of the TRICENTO G2 Transcatheter Valve System for Tricuspid Regurgitation

Intervention: : TRICENTOG2 Transcatheter Valve System for Tricuspid Regurgitation (TRICENTOG2 TVSTR) — The TRICENTO G2 TVSTR consists of a Bioprosthesis and a Delivery System including a Loading Funnel. The Bioprosthesis is an endovascular graft-like implant in combination with a lateral valve element. It is placed into the right atrium while spanning from inferior to superior vena cava leaving the native valve apparatus untouched (heterotopic approach). The TRICENTO G2 Bioprosthesis is designed to reduce the reflux of blood into the caval system during systole while allowing for forward flow during diastole. The TRICENTO G2 Bioprosthesis is delivered minimally invasive by transfemoral venous access using a catheter-based Delivery System.

: Sitz Marker Test — Colonic transit time will be assessed using the Sitz marker test, a standardized radiopaque marker method for evaluating bowel motility. Participants will swallow a capsule containing radiopaque markers, and abdominal X-rays will be obtained on day 5 to determine the number and distribution of retained markers throughout the colon. Greater marker retention indicates slower colonic transit, whereas fewer retained markers indicate faster transit and improved bowel motility.

## NCT07741721
OPtimal TIming of Staged Complete RevascularizatiON in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction With Multivessel Disease: The OPTION-STEMI2 Trial

Intervention: : In-hospital staged complete revascularization — PCI of non-IRA lesions will be performed on a separate day during the index hospitalization, at least 48 hours after PCI of the IRA. Non-IRA lesion which have equal or more than 70% diameter stenosis by visual estimation will be revascularized without FFR evaluation. Non-IRA lesion with diameter stenosis 50-69% by visual estimation will be evaluated using FFR device. In case of FFR value more than 0.8, non-IRA lesion will be deferred without PCI. If FFR value was equal or less than 0.8, non-IRA lesion will be revascularized.
: Out-of-hospital staged complete revascularization — PCI of non-IRA lesions will be performed after discharge and between 15 and 45 days of randomization. Non-IRA lesion which have equal or more than 70% diameter stenosis by visual estimation will be revascularized without FFR evaluation. Non-IRA lesion with diameter stenosis 50-69% by visual estimation will be evaluated using FFR device. In case of FFR value more than 0.8, non-IRA lesion will be deferred without PCI. If FFR value was equal or less than 0.8, non-IRA lesion will be revascularized.

## NCT07769307
Titration of Pressure Support Guided by Flow Index: A Pilot Study

Intervention: : FI-guided ventilator support adjustment — Flow index (FI)-guided pressure support (PS) titration. FI is measured non-invasively from the ventilator flow waveform at the Y-piece using 10 consecutive stable breaths. PS is adjusted to maintain FI within 2.6-4.5: PS is reduced by 2 cmH₂O if FI \< 2.6, or increased by 2 cmH₂O if FI \> 4.5. After each adjustment, a 2-minute safety assessment verifies adequate ventilation (tidal volume 4-10 mL/kg predicted body weight, respiratory rate ≤35 breaths/min, peak inspiratory pressure ≤40 cmH₂O). PS titration is performed twice daily (8:00 AM and 8:00 PM) during the intervention period. All other ventilator settings follow standard care.
: Conventional PS titration — Patients receive PSV with PS titration based on tidal volume (VT) and respiratory rate (RR). PS is adjusted to achieve VT of 6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight and RR of 20-30 breaths/min: PS is reduced by 2 cmH₂O if VT \> 8 mL/kg and/or RR \< 20 breaths/min, or increased by 2 cmH₂O if VT \< 6 mL/kg and/or RR \> 30 breaths/min. If VT is within 6-8 mL/kg, PS is not adjusted and sedation/analgesia is optimized to achieve target RR. PS titration is performed twice daily (8:00 AM and 8:00 PM) during the intervention period.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07769307

SUMMARY:

## NCT07792031
Randomized Clinical Trial: Electromagnetic Chair Therapy in Female Mixed Urinary Incontinence Compared to Standard Care (Electrostimulation With Biofeedback)

Intervention: : Electromagnetic chair therapy — Pulsed magnetic technology - electromagnetic chair therapy - has been developed for the stimulation of pelvic floor muscles. This technology was approved for marketing by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in June 1998.

For treatment, the patient is positioned in a chair. Within the chair's seat is a magnetic field generator (therapy head) that is powered and controlled by an external power unit. The output of the power unit consists of pulses of current, which can be adjusted in amplitude by the clinician. Adjusting this amplitude determines the size and strength of the magnetic field.
: Electrical stimulation therapy — ES of the pelvic floor muscles is via intravaginal electrical stimulation (IVES). This form of treatment is widely recognised and is used in clinical practice as a result of its effectiveness, despite the disadvantages of possible patient discomfort and the requirement of electrode sterilisation. IVES often uses a probe with electrodes on its surface to directly stimulate the pelvic floor muscles. It is these surface electrodes that target the pelvic floor muscles and deliver electrical impulses direct to the treatment area.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07792031

## NCT07822711
Effects of Different Stiffness Settings on Isokinetic Quadriceps Training in Children With Spinal Muscular Atrophy: A Randomized Within-Participant, Contralateral-Limb-Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Portable Isokinetic Knee Training Robot With an Individually Optimized Compliant Setting — The compliant setting will be individualized within the device's predefined safe stiffness range. At each candidate stiffness, the participant will perform five knee-extension repetitions. The stiffness producing the highest mean peak knee-extension torque while the movement remains painless, without obvious fatigue, and with a stable trajectory will be selected. The assigned limb will then train at this setting for up to 8 weeks, no more than five sessions per week. Each session will use a target angular velocity of 45 degrees per second, an individualized maximum voluntary pain-free range of motion, at least six sets of 10 extension-flexion repetitions per leg, and approximately 1 minute of rest between sets. Training volume will be matched to the contralateral limb.
: Portable Isokinetic Knee Training Robot With a Rigid Setting — The assigned limb will train with the device's predefined rigid stiffness setting for up to 8 weeks, no more than five sessions per week. Each session will use a target angular velocity of 45 degrees per second, an individualized maximum voluntary pain-free range of motion, at least six sets of 10 extension-flexion repetitions per leg, and approximately 1 minute of rest between sets. Training volume will be matched to the contralateral limb.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07822711

## NCT07891117
Multimodal Evaluation-Clinical, Radiological, Microbiological, and 3D Soft Tissue Analysis-of Dental Abutments With Different Surfaces in the Posterior Region

Intervention: : Multi-unit Abutments Xeal™ with Nobel TiUltra™ implant Parallel CC — All implant surgeries will be performed under local anesthesia. A midcrestal incision will be made with a 15C blade, followed by careful elevation of a full-thickness flap. Implant insertion will be carried out according to the manufacturer's instructions, and a Nobel TiUltra™ implant will be placed 0.5-1 mm subcrestally. Following implant placement, primary implant stability will be measured using the Osstell device. Non-engaging temporary abutment will be placed for fabrication of the temporary fixed prosthesis, which will be constructed approximately 1 mm infraocclusally. The flap will be closed primarily. After 12 weeks, the temporary prosthesis will be removed and secondary implant stability will be assessed with an Osstell device. Impressions will be taken at the abutment level, and a permanent metal-supported porcelain fixed prosthesis will be fabricated and screwed onto the Multi-unit Abutments Xeal™ with a torque of 15 Ncm.
: Conventional titanium multi-unit abutments with Nobel TiUltra™ implant Parallel CC — All implant surgeries will be performed under local anesthesia. A midcrestal incision will be made with a 15C blade, followed by careful elevation of a full-thickness flap. Implant insertion will be carried out according to the manufacturer's instructions, and a Nobel TiUltra™ implant will be placed 0.5-1 mm subcrestally. Following implant placement, primary implant stability will be measured using the Osstell device. Non-engaging temporary abutment will be placed for fabrication of the temporary fixed prosthesis, which will be constructed approximately 1 mm infraocclusally. The flap will be closed primarily. After 12 weeks, the temporary prosthesis will be removed and secondary implant stability will be assessed with an Osstell device. Impressions will be taken at the abutment level, and a permanent metal-supported porcelain fixed prosthesis will be fabricated and screwed onto the Conventional titanium multi-unit abutments with a torque of 15 Ncm.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07891117

## NCT07891702
Effect of Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation on Polysomnographic Parameters in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Prospective Interventional Study

Intervention: : Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation — Transcutaneous electrical stimulation will be delivered using an EV-906 Digital TENS/EMS device. Two 4 × 4 cm electrode patches will be placed bilaterally over the submental region, approximately halfway between the chin and the angle of the mandible. Stimulation will use a pulsed, symmetric, biphasic waveform at a frequency of 30 Hz and a phase duration of 200 microseconds, with 5-second ON and 5-second OFF cycles. Stimulation intensity will be titrated while the participant is awake to establish a tolerable sensory level. The intervention will be administered during the second overnight polysomnography session to assess its effects on polysomnographic parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07891702

Spade-Shaped Anastomosis After Laparoscopic or Robotic Proximal Gastrectomy Using Double Suture Anchoring Between the Posterior Wall of the Esophagus and the Anterior Wall of the Stomach (SPADE Operation): a Multicenter Prospective Clinical Trial.

Intervention: : Spade-Shaped Anastomosis after Laparoscopic or Robotic Proximal Gastrectomy Using Double Suture Anchoring between the Posterior Wall of the Esophagus and the Anterior Wall of the Stomac — The SPADE operation (Spade-Shaped Anastomosis) is a specialized reconstruction technique performed following a laparoscopic or robotic proximal gastrectomy for patients with upper-third early gastric cancer

* The intervention involves several key technical steps designed to preserve gastric function and prevent postoperative reflux:

Surgical Approach and Resection: The procedure begins with a laparoscopic or robotic proximal gastrectomy accompanied by D1+ lymph node dissection

* Surgeons must preserve the hepatic branch of the vagus nerve in all patients
* The esophagus is resected just above the esophagogastric junction (EGJ) using a linear stapler

Anchoring and Fixation: To create an anti-reflux mechanism, the proximal part of the residual stomach and the distal esophagus (3 cm above the transected edge) are fixed using single interrupted sutures on both sides

## NCT07892807
Thriving in a Digital World: A Mindfulness-Based Pilot to Support Sleep and Mental Health in Teens

Intervention: : Mindwire — Mindwire is an 18-day mindfulness-based, app-delivered program to support adolescents develop better coping skills and be more intentional about their phone use. In the first 4 days, participants will be listening to 5-6 short audio recordings, accompanied by text transcripts as a foundational introduction (\~4-5 minutes each), followed by booster audio recordings on Days 8 and 12. The modules will cover a variety of topics including effects of light and stress on sleep, common sleep myths, mindful wind-down routines, and stress management. Then from Days 5 to 18 (i.e., 2 weeks), participants will be asked to complete up to 3 brief surveys per day, focused on their mood and emotions. For some of these surveys, they may also be asked to complete a brief mindfulness practice. The surveys and mindfulness practices will come out to a total of approximately 30 minutes per day.

## NCT07893210
Examining the Effectiveness of the Fathers and Babies Intervention During the Perinatal Period

Intervention: : Fathers and Babies Program — FAB is a 9-session intervention divided into four modules: Introduction, Pleasant Activities, Thoughts, and Contact with Others. Fathers will be provided with a participant workbook that contains skill-based worksheets relevant to each session. Fathers will be able to choose how they would like to receive FAB: 1-on-1 delivered by a home visitor, text-based, or a combination of both. Home visitors will deliver FAB or FAB with MB based on participants' preference. FAB or FAB with MB must be delivered within 18 weeks. In the 1-on-1 modality, fathers will receive FAB through 9 in-person or virtual sessions with their home visitor. Each session lasts 20-25 minutes. The 9 sessions may occur on a weekly or bi-weekly basis. FAB content can also be delivered in a text-based format, with an initial in-person or virtual session with a home visitor to deliver session 1. The HealthySMS online platform will be used to deploy the text messages and track FAB completion by session for each father.
: Mothers and Babies Program — Mothers offered MB as part of their study participation will receive the intervention in conjunction with FAB. In the 1-on-1 MB modality, mothers will receive MB through 9 in-person or virtual sessions with their home visitor. Each session will last 20-25 minutes. The nine sessions must be delivered within 18 weeks. The MB content is divided into four modules: Introduction, Pleasant Activities, Thoughts and Contact with Others. Mothers will be provided with a participant workbook that contains skill-based worksheets relevant to each session.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07893210

## NCT06962176
Posterior Mitral Isthmus Line With Vein of Marshall Ethanolisation Compared With Anterior Mitral Lines in Patients With Persistent Atrial Fibrillation

Intervention: : Anterior Mitral Line Ablation — First pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is performed - either as a first-time isolation (index procedure) or a re-isolation (in repeat procedures). Then a linear lesion is created on the anterior wall of the left atrium, from the roof line to the mitral annulus.
: Posterior Mitral Isthmus Ablation with Vein of Marshall Ethanol Infusion — Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is systematically carried out before any additional ablation lines are created - either as initial isolation or re-isolation. In this group the posterior mitral isthmus, a region between the left inferior pulmonary vein and the mitral annulus, is targeted. Endocardial ablation using a dual energy catheter (RF and PF) is combined with ethanol infusion in the vein of Marshall (VOM), which ablates the adjacent epicardial tissue to enhance lesion durability.

## NCT07045844
The Effects of Different Enteral Feeding Regimens on Necrotizing Enterocolitis, Mortality, and Neurodevelopment in Very Preterm Infants: A Multicenter Double-Randomized Trial

Intervention: : Pasteurized Donor Milk for Insufficient Breastfeeding — Participants receive pasteurized donor human milk (pHDM) as supplemental feeding when the clinician determines maternal milk supply is insufficient.

Randomization 1 will occur when the clinician determines that supplemental feeding is required due to insufficient breast milk supply.
: Preterm Formula for Insufficient Breastfeeding — Participants receive preterm formula (PTF) as supplemental feeding when the clinician determines maternal milk supply is insufficient.

Randomization 1 will occur when the clinician determines that supplemental feeding is required due to insufficient breast milk supply.
: Routine fortification — Randomization 2 will be conducted when the total daily intake of human milk (including own mother's milk \[OMM\] and/or donor pasteurized human milk \[pHDM\] ) reaches between 60-120 mL/kg
: Rescue fortification — Randomization 2 will be conducted: Add fortifiers when the infant meets predefined criteria for growth faltering (Preterm infants exhibit a sustained decline in growth velocity for weight, length, or head circumference, demonstrated by a downward crossing of centiles on growth curves, despite tolerating and consuming at least 180 mL/kg/day of breast milk or formula. Blood urea levels in these infants remain consistently below 1.5 mmol/L, and there are no severe complications such as active sepsis or the need for vasoactive medications to maintain circulatory stability. Chronic sodium depletion has also been ruled out, as this condition alone can lead to growth failure. Additionally, preterm infants are unable to tolerate high-volume feeding of 180 mL/kg/day due to specific reasons, such as severe gastroesophageal reflux or the presence of a high-output stoma following surgical procedures).
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07045844

## NCT07340021
Effects of Neuromuscular Warm-up Versus Conventional Warm-up Protocols on Dynamic Balance and Strength Among Recreational Gym Population

Intervention: : NM Warm-up — The neuromuscular warm-up was performed four times per week for six weeks, with each session lasting approximately 10 to12 minutes at light to moderate intensity. The intervention consisted of single-leg balance exercises with reach tasks, bosu mini squats with controlled tempo, core stabilization exercises such as front and side planks, and agility-based movements including lateral shuffles and hops. Exercise difficulty was progressively increased by altering base of support, movement speed, and task complexity. The sequence was designed to improve motor control, balance reactions, and force production before the main workout. Dynamic balance and strength outcomes were assessed at baseline and after completion of the intervention.
: Conventional Warm-up — Participants in the control group completed the conventional warm-up four times per week for six weeks, with each session lasting about 10 to 12 minutes. The warm-up began with light aerobic activity, such as treadmill jogging or stationary cycling, to gently raise heart rate and body temperature. This was followed by dynamic mobility and stretching exercises, including leg swings, arm circles, hip rotations, , body-weight squats, and dynamic stretches for the hamstrings and calves also of upper body dynamic stretches . Overall, the conventional warm-up aimed to prepare the muscles and joints for exercise but did not specifically target neuromuscular activation, balance, or movement control.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07340021

## NCT07571369
Impact of Dual Task Therapeutic Exercises on Stress Modulation and Dynamic Balance in University Students

Intervention: : Dynamic balance exercises — Participants perform a structured set of dynamic balance exercises under single-task conditions (motor task only). Exercises include:

1. Controlled Backward Walking (CBW): Walk backward in a straight line (10 meters) using a toe-heel strike pattern; maintain upright trunk, head forward, arms naturally at sides.
2. Controlled Lateral Dynamic Stepping (CLDS): Step sideways along a 10 meter path; feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly flexed, hands clasped at chest; gaze fixed forward.
3. Single-Leg Forward Reach (SLFR): Stand on one limb, hands crossed over chest; reach the non-standing leg forward to touch the floor with toes, return without losing balance. 10 repetitions per leg.
4. Single-Leg Lateral Reach (SLSR): Same as SLFR but reaching sideways (lateral abduction). 10 repetitions per leg.
5. Dynamic Tandem Gait (DTG): Walk heel-to-toe in a straight line (10 meters) with hands crossed over chest; gaze fixed forward
: Control group — Control Group: Participants will receive supervised, low-intensity exercises consisting of ankle pumps, seated knee flexion and extension, shoulder circles, and gentle cervical range-of-motion exercises. Sessions will be conducted for a duration and frequency consistent with the approved study protocol.
: Dual task exercises — Arm B: Dual-Task Therapeutic Exercise Group

Intervention Type: Other (Dual-Task Training)

Intervention Name: Dual-Task Therapeutic Exercise

Description:

Participants perform exactly the same dynamic balance exercises as Arm A, but simultaneously with a secondary cognitive task (dual-task condition). The cognitive task is performed throughout the duration of each balance exercise. Cognitive tasks are varied across sessions to maintain engagement and avoid habituation, and include:

* Verbal Fluency Task: e.g., "Name as many words as you can starting with the letter 'S'" or "Name as many animals/fruits/cities."
* Arithmetic Task: e.g., "Count backwards from 100 by 7" or "Subtract 3 from 50, then 3 from that number, and so on."
* Working Memory Task: The therapist reads a list of numbers or words; the participant recalls them in reverse order (digits backward).
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07571369

## NCT07893392
Phase II Study of Primary Tumor Resection and Selective Lymph Node Dissection Followed by Postoperative Radiotherapy for Biliary Tract Cancer With Lymph Node Metastases

Intervention: : Primary Tumor Resection and Selective Lymph Node Dissection — Patients will undergo primary tumor resection with selective lymph node dissection. During surgery, regional and retroperitoneal lymph nodes will be explored, and lymph nodes that are technically amenable to surgical resection will be selectively dissected. Metastatic lymph nodes that cannot be safely or completely resected because of local invasion or because they extend beyond the feasible surgical dissection field will not be surgically resected and will subsequently be treated with postoperative radiotherapy.
: Postoperative Radiotherapy — All patients will receive postoperative radiotherapy using intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) or volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT).

For patients undergoing R0/R1 resection, the high-risk tumor bed, including narrow-margin or lymph node-positive tumor beds, will receive 55-65 Gy in 20-25 fractions, while elective nodal regions will receive 40-45 Gy in 20-25 fractions. Radiotherapy to the primary tumor bed may be omitted when the surgical margin is considered adequate.

For patients undergoing R2 resection, the high-risk tumor bed will receive 55-65 Gy in 20-25 fractions, residual metastatic lymph nodes will receive 60-70 Gy in 20-25 fractions, and elective nodal regions will receive 40-45 Gy in 20-25 fractions. Radiotherapy to the primary tumor bed may be omitted when the surgical margin is considered adequate.
: Capecitabine or S-1 — For patients undergoing R0/R1 resection, capecitabine or S-1 will be administered concurrently with radiotherapy for 2 cycles, followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy. Capecitabine will be administered at 1,600 mg/m² on Days 1-14 every 21 days during radiotherapy and 2,000 mg/m² on Days 1-14 every 21 days for 6 subsequent cycles. For patients intolerant to capecitabine, S-1 will be substituted: concurrent S-1 40-50 mg twice daily on Days 1-28, every 42 days for 1 cycle, followed by maintenance S-1 40-60 mg twice daily on Days 1-28, every 42 days for 3 cycles.

For patients undergoing R2 resection, capecitabine or S-1, with or without a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor, will be administered concurrently with radiotherapy, followed by maintenance treatment with the same regimen until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07893392

SUMMARY:

Intervention: : IMB Model-Guided Health Education Intervention — Participants allocated to the intervention arm will receive a structured, face-to-face health literacy intervention in addition to usual hypertension care. The intervention will be guided by the IMB model, which posits that health behavior change is determined by adequate information, sufficient personal and the acquisition of relevant behavioral skills. The information component will aim to improve participants' and their significant others' health literacy regarding hypertension and its management. The motivation component will focus on strengthening personal and social motivation for medication adherence and healthy self-care behaviors. Intervention: : Gait parameter assessment — A Biodex Gait Trainer 3 (BIODEX MEDICAL SYSTEMS, INC., New York, NY, model NO. 601-1-M90, EN 60601- 1 USA), is a device which is used to assess the spatiotemporal gait parameters of patients . It consists of a treadmill with an instrumented deck that monitors and records kinematic gait parameters including gait speed, step cycle, step length, and time on each foot (step symmetry). The patient will instructed to stand on the treadmill holding on handrails to ensure safety. Each patient will be asked to walk continuously for 3 minutes, till the evaluation session ended, and the gait trainer slow down gradually until it stopped. Three successive trials will be done for each patient. The mean value of each variable of spatiotemporal parameters of gait \[walking speed (meters per seconds), step cycle (cycle per second), step length (meter), and time on each foot (seconds)\] will be recorded.

Treatment regimens are determined by multidisciplinary review. Monthly blood sampling is performed during adjuvant therapy. Based on current evidence, treatment de-escalation based solely on ctDNA status is not supported in lung cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy. Thus, patients achieving pCR with negative ctDNA at both predefined timepoints receive no adjuvant therapy. Blood is collected at routine follow-up visits, and adjuvant therapy is initiated upon ctDNA seroconversion to positive.

Intervention: : Nanohydroxyapatite Varnish Application — Preparation: Professional prophylaxis of target labial surface with non-fluoridated pumice and rubber cup, followed by partial isolation using cheek retractors, high-volume suction, and cotton rolls.

Application: A dime-sized amount of premixed 8.6% nano-HAp varnish is dispensed on a mixing pad and swept uniformly across the labial surface using a soft brush applicator over 15 to 30 seconds.

: Sodium Fluoride Varnish Application — Preparation: Identical professional prophylaxis with non-fluoridated pumice, rinsing, and moisture control isolation.

## NCT07894523
Clinical and Radiographic Evaluation of DIA-ROOT BIO MTA as an Indirect Pulp Capping Agent in Young Permanent Molars

Intervention: : Dia-Root Bio MTA Indirect Pulp Capping — Preparation: Administration of 4% Articaine local anesthesia with epinephrine, rubber dam isolation, high-speed cavity preparation to non-carious dentin at lateral walls, and selective excavation of soft carious dentin at the pulpal floor using a manual excavator (leaving firm affected dentin). Cavity flushed with saline for 10 seconds and air-dried.

Capping \& Restoration: Dia-Root Bio MTA mixed with sterile distilled water (0.225g : 0.5g powder ratio) for 30 seconds, placed over residual dentin at 3-4 mm thickness, and condensed with a moist cotton pellet. Cavity sealed immediately with glass ionomer cement base (Nova Glass) and restored with composite resin (Tetric N Ceram).
: MTA Plus Indirect Pulp Capping — Preparation: Identical local anesthesia, rubber dam isolation, lateral wall caries excavation, and selective soft dentin excavation at the pulpal floor, saline flush, and air-drying.

## NCT07894614
Ablation Versus Non-ablation Strategies for Non-puerperal Mastitis: A Prospective Real-world Registry Study

Intervention: : Ablation — Under real-time ultrasound guidance, an ablation needle (radiofrequency electrode, microwave antenna, or laser fiber) is precisely punctured into the center of the lesion. The corresponding energy generator is then connected with parameters configured, and energy delivery is initiated to rapidly raise local tissue temperature above 60 °C, inducing coagulative necrosis of cells via thermal biological effects. The ablation zone is continuously monitored by imaging during the procedure; needle position or parameters are adjusted when necessary to ensure complete lesion coverage. Energy output is terminated once the pre-set ablation margin is achieved, and the ablation needle is withdrawn.
: Observation — Basic symptomatic treatment: Patients receive symptomatic care. Glucocorticoid therapy: Prednisone (5 mg), methylprednisolone (4 mg) or prednisone acetate (5 mg) starts at 0.5 mg/(kg·d). After 2-week maintenance, doses are gradually tapered; low-dose maintenance (2.5-5.0 mg/d) continues 4-8 weeks per symptoms and tolerability.

Anti-tuberculosis therapy: Oral rifampicin, isoniazid and ethambutol for 6-9 months.

Surgical resection: Pre-operative ultrasound maps lesions. Local or general anesthesia is used. Inflammatory lesions and sinus tracts are completely excised with maximal preservation of normal breast parenchyma.Intra-operative hemostasis and saline irrigation are done; primary closure or open drainage depends on wound status. Post-operative symptomatic care and wound dressing are provided.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07894614

SUMMARY:

## NCT07895277
Study of Imaging Evolution of Pulmonary Nodules and Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Diagnostic and Management Strategies

Intervention: : AI-Assisted Longitudinal CT Assessment and Pulmonary Nodule Management — AI software analyzes serial clinically acquired chest CT scans to match pulmonary nodules, quantify changes in volume and solid components, and provide malignancy or invasiveness risk estimates. Intervention-arm clinicians review the AI report alongside CT images during management consultations. The baseline report is targeted within one working day after randomization. The same locked model is reapplied to clinically indicated follow-up CT scans during the 24-month intervention period. Clinicians retain responsibility for final decisions; AI findings cannot independently override clinically indicated evaluation. If processing fails or images are unsuitable, usual care proceeds. Both arms follow the same structured nodule-management pathway, but the control arm has no access to trial AI reports.

## NCT07895290
Diagnosis of Infectious Pneumonia and Detection of Unusual Infections Using Medical Imaging and Artificial Intelligence

Intervention: : CT-Based AI Decision Support for Pneumonia — A locked CT-based artificial intelligence (AI) clinical decision-support system will analyze chest CT scans obtained as part of routine clinical care for patients with pneumonia. The system provides probabilities for predefined pathogen classes, quantitative assessment of pulmonary lesion extent, longitudinal changes when prior CT scans are available, and estimates of short-term clinical deterioration risk.

For patients assigned to the intervention group, the AI-generated report will be made available to treating clinicians, with a target availability within one hour after randomization. Clinicians will review the AI findings alongside the original CT images and other clinical information within two hours and document any resulting changes in diagnosis, further testing, treatment, or monitoring.

The AI system supports clinical decision-making but does not replace physician judgment. Additional CT scans are not required, and subsequent clinically indicated scans may also be analyzed.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07895290

## NCT07895979
The Efficacy of an IADL-based Non-immersive Virtual Reality Training Program to Enhance ADL Performance and Cognitive Function for Persons at Risk of Dementia

Intervention: : Daily Life VR Training — Delivered on a 16-inch touchscreen computer incorporating touch, handwriting recognition, and voice interaction. The software features three core daily living themes with 3 to 4 sequential sub-tasks each, graded across 5 to 8 difficulty levels:

1. Holiday Reunion Dinner Preparation: Checking home inventory to create a shopping list, supermarket shopping while filtering out audio promotional distractions, price comparison and checkout calculation, and following cooking sequences.
2. Health Management: Operating a hospital registration kiosk under time and step constraints, remembering physician and pharmacist instructions during a clinic visit, and organizing a medication pillbox.
3. Travel Planning: Packing luggage spatially, navigating bus and train schedules/platforms, reacting to unexpected events (e.g., retrieving blown-away luggage), and problem-solving during travel emergencies (e.g., lost items or suspended train services).
: Non-Conditional Game VR Training — Uses commercial digital cognitive games consisting of 22 short mini-games (under 2 minutes each) across five domains: attention, memory, mathematics, general cognition, and language, without real-life situational integration.
: Traditional Cognitive Training — Uses structured commercial board games and tabletop activities facilitated by an occupational therapist, focusing on a specific cognitive domain each week (attention, working memory, visuospatial skills, executive function, cognitive flexibility, and language).

A Phase II Study of Ivarmacitinib Combined With Camrelizumab and Fruquintinib for Patients With Metastatic Colorectal Cancer After Failure of Second-line or Later Treatment

Intervention: : Ivarmacitinib + Camrelizumab + Fruquintinib — Participants will receive treatment for up to 1 year in three phases. Phase 1 (lead-in phase): Ivarmacitinib 4 mg orally once daily for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (combination induction phase): Ivarmacitinib 4 mg orally once daily, camrelizumab 200 mg intravenously once every 3 weeks, and fruquintinib 5 mg orally once daily for 14 days followed by 7 days off treatment.

Phase 3 (maintenance phase): Camrelizumab 200 mg intravenously once every 3 weeks in combination with fruquintinib 5 mg orally once daily for 14 days followed by 7 days off treatment, for 15 cycles.

Treatment will continue until completion of the planned treatment period, disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or another criterion for treatment discontinuation is met. Tumor response will be assessed according to RECIST criteria every 6 weeks (after every two cycles of immunotherapy). Participants with progressive disease (PD) will discontinue study treatment.

## NCT07602296
Effect of Transcranial Photobiomodulation on Clinical Symptoms, Quality of Life and Cerebral Connectivity Modifications in Dementia With Lewy Bodies

Intervention: : LUCIOLE CAP — The LUCIOLE Cap is a medical device (without CE mark) designed for transcranial photobiomodulation (PBM). The cap was developed specifically for this purpose by the CLINATEC Endowment Fund (FDC), and it has not been used in any clinical investigation before. The LUCIOLE Cap will be used for the first time in this study with patients diagnosed with Dementia with Lewy bodies.

The LUCIOLE cap is a non-invasive device that delivers PBM to the brain by shining light through the skin and bone. The LEDs emit near-infrared-light at a wavelength of 810 nm, with an illumination power of up to 8W (\~40mW/cm²).

For safety, the cap must only be used in the room chosen by the study investigator during the first home visit. It must be used in a dry environment, away from sources of water or moisture, avoiding direct sunlight, and at a room temperature between 5°C and 27.5°C.
: LUCIOLE CAP (sham version) — The CLINATEC Endowment Fund (FDC) designed this sham cap exclusively for scientific studies. It is built specifically to provide an accurate comparison against the active cap. This precise control allows investigators to clearly evaluate whether the active LUCIOLE cap delivers true, measurable benefits.

The sham cap mimics the active LUCIOLE cap's operational characteristics and heat output without delivering actual PBM. The devices look identical and are distinguishable only by their serial numbers. This internal difference in electronics and firmware guarantees that both clinical investigators and participants remain blinded to the treatment allocation.

For safety, the cap must only be used in the room chosen by the study investigator during the first home visit. It must be used in a dry environment, away from sources of water or moisture, avoiding direct sunlight, and at a room temperature between 5°C and 27.5°C.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07602296

SUMMARY:

The automated fluid management system continuously monitors and manages intravesical pressure while actively evacuating tissue to prevent clogging. ## NCT07763782
Optimizing Venous Leg Ulcer Healing Via Dose-Response Structured Calf Muscle Pump Activation Strategies Versus Unsupervised Home Walks

Intervention: : Dose-Response Structured CMP Activation — Progression Protocol (The Dose-Response) Weeks 1-4 (Activation Phase): Focuses on establishing baseline mobility. Ankle ROM Drills: 3 sets of 15 repetitions of passive and active dorsiflexion/plantar flexion stretches utilizing an inelastic stretching strap. Goal: Overcome joint stiffness to reach \>10° of passive dorsiflexion. Seated CMP Loading: Seated heel raises with resistive elastic bands (15 repetitions, 4 sets).

Weeks 5-8 (Hypertrophy \& Ejection Phase): Focuses on building muscle pump volume.

Standing Closed-Kinetic Chain Exercises: Standing bodyweight heel raises performed on a step to allow a deep negative heel deficit (eccentric loading). 4 sets of 12 repetitions. Incline Ergometry: 15 minutes of continuous stationary cycling or treadmill walking at a 5% to 8% incline to force a natural heel-strike and powerful toe-off phase.

Weeks 9-12 (Power \& Hemodynamic Clearance Phase): Focuses on clearing pooled blood under high pressure.

Resisted Plantarflexion: Single-leg standing hee
: Active Control — Patients were issued a medical-grade wrist-worn pedometer and a matching ankle sensor. The device display was blinded (blacked out) to prevent active self-biasing or behavioral modification based on step count numbers. Data was downloaded retroactively by researchers at bi-weekly clinic visits to measure real-world gait speeds, step counts, total active time, and spatial asymmetries without the patient altering their natural routine. No constraints were placed on gait modifications. If the patient guards their wound by walking flat-footed or shuffling, the behavior is recorded but not corrected, providing a true representation of unguided real-world walking mechanics.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07763782

Following harvesting, the RA graft is prepared without fasciotomy or VG solution predilation.

## NCT07896343
Defining Orbitofrontal Circuit Function in Health and Depression

Intervention: : Approach-Avoidance Decision-Making Task — A computerized, gamified approach-avoidance decision-making task built in the Unity game engine and presented on a laptop at the bedside during inpatient sEEG monitoring. On each trial, the participant views a virtual corridor containing a reward offer (0-7 treasure chests) and a punishment offer (0-4 bombs) and indicates by button press whether to approach the corridor, with probabilistic gain and loss outcomes, or avoid it, with a neutral outcome. Reward and punishment magnitudes are varied in pseudorandomized order across 220 trials per session (\~20 minutes). Choices and reaction times are recorded and synchronized with intracranial neural recordings at millisecond precision. The task serves as an experimental probe of the neural and behavioral mechanisms of approach-avoidance decision-making; it is not a treatment, and no therapeutic effect is expected. Task code is openly available (github.com/cstarkweather).
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07896343

Intervention: : AI-Simulation Programme — Five individual AI-simulation cases on a dedicated psychiatric simulation platform, one case per week over five consecutive weeks, each lasting about 15-20 minutes and delivered as a low-stakes, ungraded learning activity after a brief orientation. Cases are delivered in a fixed order from least to most emotionally demanding: major depression with suicide risk, mania/bipolar disorder, schizophrenia with hallucinations, substance use disorder with withdrawal, and borderline personality disorder with self-harm. Each case includes a timed structured interview with a simulated patient in Egyptian colloquial Arabic, a Mental State Examination checklist, a standardized (fixed) stigma-trigger statement, a first-attempt response, automated AI feedback, a retry opportunity, and a performance summary. The platform retains no conversational content.

## NCT07896902
Xenon MRI to Evaluate Changes to Lung Function Following Bronchoscopic Treatment of Air Trapping in Emphysema

Intervention: : Hyperpolarized Xenon MRI — Hyperpolarized Xenon MRI (HP ¹²#Xe) is a radiation-free imaging technique that boosts signal strength to create high-resolution images of how gas moves through the lungs. By tracking inhaled gas across separate breath-holds, it measures airflow blockage, tissue transfer efficiency, and gas uptake by red blood cells, while a washout test maps how well the lungs clear gas. It has been applied to characterize pulmonary impairment in COPD and emphysema and to detect regional ventilation changes following bronchoscopic interventions.
: Apreo BREATHE Airway Scaffold — The experimental treatment involves placement of up to 6 Apreo BREATHE Airway Scaffolds (up to 3 per lung), in a single procedure using bronchoscopy and fluoroscopy. Treatment group subjects will also receive optimal medical management (OMM). The BREATHE Airway Scaffold implant procedure occurs under the BREATHE-3 main study. This procedure is not part of the BREATHE-Xe study, which focuses on changes in regional ventilation.

## NCT07899034
Effects of Music Therapy on Sleep Quality in Post-Stroke Patients: A Clinical Trial at the San Cecilio University Hospital

Intervention: : Music therapy — Intervention Characteristics:

* Duration: each music therapy session will last 60 minutes
* Setting: the sessions will be administered during at night shift in the Neurology Department of the Hospital Universitario Clínico San Cecilio (HUCSC).
* Frequency: daily sessions will be administered during the participant's hospitalization, whenever the participant's clinical condition allows.
* Type of music: the selected music will consist of slow rhythms (60-80 bpm) and soft sounds, avoiding abrupt changes. Pieces in lower pitches and with flowing melodies have been shown to facilitate the transition to sleep, while avoiding elements that may stimulate the listener, such as lyrics or pronounced rythms.
* Method of delivery: low-intensity speakers will be used in dimly lit environments to expose participants to the music therapy intervention.
