## NCT07899606
SITE SPECIFIC DRILLING PROTOCOL BASED ON DIGITAL EYE®-ASSISTED BONE DENSITY CLASSIFICATION AND PRIMARY DENTAL IMPLANT STABILITY. SINGLE- ARM PROSPECTIVE CLINICAL STUDY

Intervention: : R2GATE Digital EYE-Assisted Site-Specific Drilling Protocol — Digitally guided implant placement will be planned and performed for thirty bounded edentulous maxillary and thirty mandibular molar healed sites. Pre-operative CBCT Images of the maxillary and mandibular jaws of the recruited patients will be acquired. Images will be obtained in DICOM format and exported to the software for pre-operative digital implant planning.

R2GATE® Digital EYE® is used to assess bone density at the planned implant site and generate a site-specific drilling recommendation. The osteotomy is prepared according to the software-recommended drilling sequence, with the use or omission of an optional final drill recorded when applicable. Primary implant stability is measured immediately after placement using insertion torque and resonance frequency analysis, reported as the implant stability quotient (ISQ). A digitally designed surgical guide is used to guide placement of a MegaGen AnyRidge® dental implant.
: R2GATE® Digital EYE® Implant Planning Software — R2GATE® Digital EYE® software is used to assess bone density at the planned implant site and generate a site-specific drilling recommendation. Preoperative CBCT images are imported into the software for digital implant planning. The recommended osteotomy drilling sequence is followed during implant placement.
: MEGA ISQ® - Implant Stability Measurement Device — The MEGA ISQ® device is used to assess primary dental implant stability immediately after implant placement using resonance frequency analysis (RFA). Measurements are recorded as implant stability quotient (ISQ) values in the specified measurement directions, and the readings are averaged to obtain the mean ISQ for each implant.
: Insertion Torque Measurement — A dental implant surgical motor (MEG Engine® II ) with torque measurement is used during implant placement to record insertion torque, expressed in N·cm, as an indicator of primary implant stability. The insertion torque value is recorded for each implant immediately after placement.
: UNC-15 Probe Depth Measurement Device — The UNC-15 Probe is used to assess the clinically achieved implant placement depth. The measured clinical depth is recorded and compared with the digitally planned implant depth to evaluate the accuracy of implant placement and the discrepancy between planned and achieved depths.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07899606

Effects of Perturbation-Based Versus Conventional Balance Training on Reactive Stepping Ability in Patients With Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy

Intervention: : Perturbation-Based Balance Training (PBBT) — Participants will receive routine physical therapy (7 minutes of warm-up, 6 minutes of rest, and 7 minutes of cool-down) along with perturbation-based balance training for 8 weeks, with 3 supervised sessions per week (24 sessions, 60 minutes each). After a 2-week shared familiarization phase (weeks 1-2), participants will receive manually delivered, repeated exposure to unexpected and externally imposed postural perturbations by a physical therapist in standing position on stable and unstable surfaces (weeks 3-8). Perturbations will progress from anterior and posterior to multi-directional and randomized, and from standing tasks to walking, uneven surfaces, and dual-task conditions, increasing from 10 to 15 perturbations per session. A support bar and pre-session blood glucose monitoring will be used for safety.
: Conventional Balance Training (CBT) — Participants will receive routine physical therapy (7 minutes of warm-up, 6 minutes of rest, and 7 minutes of cool-down) along with conventional balance training for 8 weeks, with 3 supervised sessions per week (24 sessions, 60 minutes each). After a 2-week shared familiarization phase (weeks 1-2), participants will be trained for balance with eyes open and eyes closed in various conditions on stable and unstable surfaces, with no manual perturbations (weeks 3-8). Training will progress from foam-pad standing and weight shifting to functional gait tasks, obstacle negotiation, stair negotiation, and dual-task walking. A support bar and pre-session blood glucose monitoring will be used for safety.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07902297

SUMMARY:

## NCT07409649
Influence of Intermittent Hypoxia on Loop Gain in Healthy Subjects

Intervention: : Intermittent hypoxia — The volunteer will remain at rest in the hypoxic chamber, experiencing intermittent hypoxic conditions cyclically every 6 minutes. During one third of the cycle, they will be exposed to hypoxia in order to reduce SpO₂ to between 85% and 90%. Then, during two thirds of the cycle, they will receive oxygenation at a rate of 1 L/min (with possible subject-dependent modulations), with the aim of achieving an SpO₂ of greater than 95%.

To make the hypoxia intermittent, the volunteer will also be given a medium-concentration oxygen mask that provides intermittent airflow, controlled by the D-6341 mass flow controller.
: Normoxia — The participant will remain at rest in the hypoxic chamber under normoxic conditions. To prevent the volunteer from becoming aware of the conditions to which they are exposed, an air flow rate of 1 L/min will be used to simulate intermittent oxygenation.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07409649

SUMMARY:

## NCT07883382
An Exploratory Study of Gecacitinib in the Peri-Transplant Period for Patients With Myeloid Neoplasms and Myelofibrosis Undergoing Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation

Intervention: : gecacitinib Hydrochloride Tablets — gecacitinib is administered orally, starting 13 weeks before allo-HSCT. Starting dose is based on baseline platelet count: 100 mg twice daily (BID) if platelets ≥50×10\^9/L, or 50 mg BID if platelets \<50×10\^9/L.The dose will be reduced to 50 mg BID beginning on day -7 (1 week before transplantation) and maintained at this dose during conditioning and transplantation. After hematopoietic reconstitution (PLT ≥50×10\^9/L and ANC ≥0.5×10\^9/L), the dose is increased to 100 mg BID for 12 weeks, then tapered to 50 mg BID for another 12 weeks before discontinuation.

Dose adjustments are made based on adverse events and hematologic parameters, with a maximum dose of 100 mg BID and minimum of 50 mg once daily (QD).
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07883382

## NCT07192601
Developing an E-Cigarette Cessation Intervention for Hispanic/Latina(o) Youth in Florida

Intervention: : E-cigarette Cessation Manual — The intervention is grounded in an empirically supported psychosocial smoking cessation program (i.e., Cognitive Behavior Therapy \[CBT\]; Vinci, 2020), as well as a manualized CBT e-cigarette intervention for adolescents and young adults (Kong et al., 2017; Kong et al., 2021). The structure and content of the manual were further informed by themes identified through focus groups. The newly developed BReATHE Program will consist of six 60-minute group sessions. "Building Knowledge for Change" focuses on nicotine vaping psychoeducation. "Recognizing the Triangle" introduces the cognitive triangle. "Anticipating Triggers" offers tools to cope with internal and external triggers to vape. "Tranquil Minds" offers relaxation techniques to manage negative emotions. "Healthy Communication" teaches clients more effective ways to communicate. "Educate Others" consists of reviewing skills and planning for the graduation ceremony where youth will teach family members what they learned.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07192601

## NCT07409649
Influence of Intermittent Hypoxia on Loop Gain in Healthy Subjects

Intervention: : Intermittent hypoxia — The volunteer will remain at rest in the hypoxic chamber, experiencing intermittent hypoxic conditions cyclically every 6 minutes. During one third of the cycle, they will be exposed to hypoxia in order to reduce SpO₂ to between 85% and 90%. Then, during two thirds of the cycle, they will receive oxygenation at a rate of 1 L/min (with possible subject-dependent modulations), with the aim of achieving an SpO₂ of greater than 95%.

To make the hypoxia intermittent, the volunteer will also be given a medium-concentration oxygen mask that provides intermittent airflow, controlled by the D-6341 mass flow controller.
: Normoxia — The participant will remain at rest in the hypoxic chamber under normoxic conditions. To prevent the volunteer from becoming aware of the conditions to which they are exposed, an air flow rate of 1 L/min will be used to simulate intermittent oxygenation.

## NCT07497269
Pulsed vs Conventional Radiofrequency of the Ganglion Impar for Coccydynia: A Prospective Randomized Trial

Intervention: : Pulsed Radiofrequency — Once the needle is properly positioned along the sacrococcygeal disc line, 1 mL of radiopaque contrast is injected. The needle placement is confirmed in the lateral fluoroscopic view as a comma-shaped spread in the retroperitoneal space.

Radiofrequency interventions on the ganglion impar are performed using a radiofrequency generator. A 22G radiofrequency needle (0.7×98.6 mm) with a 10 mm exposed active tip is used. Before performing the ablation, tissue impedance and motor and sensory responses (motor and sensory stimulation) are checked. The expected tissue impedance is \<500 ohms. Sensory paresthesia at \<1 V and 50 Hz is observed around the sacrococcygeal region. Pulsed RFA is applied at 42 °C for 4 minutes after stimulation.
: Conventional Radiofrequency — Once the needle is properly positioned along the sacrococcygeal disc line, 1 mL of radiopaque contrast is injected. The needle placement is confirmed in the lateral fluoroscopic view as a comma-shaped spread in the retroperitoneal space.

Radiofrequency interventions on the ganglion impar are performed using a radiofrequency generator. A 22G radiofrequency needle (0.7×98.6 mm) with a 10 mm exposed active tip is used. Before performing the ablation, tissue impedance and motor and sensory responses (motor and sensory stimulation) are checked. The expected tissue impedance is \<500 ohms. Sensory paresthesia at \<1 V and 50 Hz is observed around the sacrococcygeal region. Neuroablation is applied for 2 cycles of 90 seconds at 80 °C.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07497269

## NCT07598799
Rapid Local Ischemic Postconditioning Following Successful Recanalization After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Large Ischemic Core Stroke

Intervention: : High-dose RL-IPostC — For acute anterior circulation with large core ischemic stroke patients who achieve successful vessel recanalization (mTICI 2b/3) after thrombectomy, within 5 minutes, the balloon guide catheter (BGC) is positioned in the straight segment of the ipsilateral internal carotid artery at the C1-C2 level, avoiding the carotid sinus. Repetitive balloon inflations (2 minutes) to block blood flow followed by deflations (2 minutes) to restore blood flow (for 4 cycles) are performed. After the first BGC inflation, confirmation of antegrade flow blockade in the internal carotid artery is required. At the end of the cycle, angiography is performed to confirm vessel patency.
: Low-dose RL-IPostC — For acute anterior circulation with large core ischemic stroke patients who achieve successful vessel recanalization (mTICI 2b/3) after thrombectomy, within 5 minutes, the balloon guide catheter (BGC) is positioned in the straight segment of the ipsilateral internal carotid artery at the C1-C2 level, avoiding the carotid sinus. Repetitive balloon inflations (15 seconds) to block blood flow followed by deflations (15 seconds) to restore blood flow (for 5 cycles) are performed. After the first BGC inflation, confirmation of antegrade flow blockade in the internal carotid artery is required. At the end of the cycle, angiography is performed to confirm vessel patency.

## NCT07778966
Alabama Womb to Heart Solution: A Community-Based Cardiovascular Health Intervention After Hypertension in Pregnancy

Intervention: : Alabama Womb to Heart Solution (AW2H) Community Health Worker (CHW) Program — Six-month community health worker (CHW) program delivered in partnership with ConnectionHealth. Visit/contact frequency: Approximately 2 times/week for weeks 1-5, weekly for weeks 6-12, and monthly for weeks 13-26; visits may be in person or virtual (phone/video). CHWs coach home blood pressure monitoring with American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)-concordant escalation guidance, reinforce antihypertensive medication adherence, educate on postpartum danger signs and long-term cardiovascular risk, remind about postpartum and pediatric visits, counsel on breastfeeding and contraception, coach on American Heart Association (AHA) Life's Essential 8 behaviors, assist with scheduling and attending a primary care appointment, provide mother-baby guidance (safe sleep, immunizations, developmental milestones), and offer trauma-informed emotional support.

Intervention: : TNP-2092 for injection — Starting on D1, administer by intra-articular injection either once daily or once weekly. Participants in Arm A will receive once-daily dosing for 14 days, and participants in Arm B and Arm C will receive once-weekly dosing for 4 weeks. Doses should be administered at approximately the same time whenever possible (no more than 1 hour earlier or later than the time of the first dose).
: Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection — Participants receive empiric treatment with vancomycin 1 g administered via IV infusion every 12 hours (q12h). For participants aged 65 years or older, the vancomycin dose may be adjusted to 0.5 g q12h; during the study, it may also be adjusted according to renal function.
: Oral antibiotics — After 14 days of IV infusion, participants who meet the criteria for IV to oral switch may switch to oral antibiotic treatment (minocycline or levofloxacin, as determined by the investigator). After 7 days of IV infusion, if IV administration cannot be continued due to tolerability or other reasons, participants may also switch to oral antibiotic treatment if they meet the criteria for IV to oral switch. Oral treatment lasts 56-63 days and combined IV plus oral treatment lasts a total of 10 weeks (70 days).

* Levofloxacin tablets: 0.5 g (1 tablet) orally once daily, taken within 1 hour before breakfast, for 56-63 days.
* Minocycline hydrochloride capsules: administered orally twice daily; the first dose is 200 mg (2 capsules), and all subsequent doses are 100 mg (1 capsule), for 56-63 days.
: Appropriate intravenous and/or oral antibiotics — The investigator will select appropriate intravenous and/or oral antibiotics based on the participant's condition and with reference to domestic and international guidelines, to be continued for 10 weeks (70 days).

## NCT07900893
Cognitive Neurocomputational Task Reliability and Clinical Applications Consortium

Intervention: : Motion Perception Task — Assesses updating of beliefs from new sensory inputs with prior knowledge via perceiving direction changes in random dot motion stimuli
: Sine Wave Speech Task — Measures the degree to which overweighting of prior beliefs impacts processing of sensory inputs (detection of speech).
: Volatility Task — Measures the updating of priors about the location of a bag drop from a helicopter when the location changes (prediction errors).
: Choice Probabilistic Reversal Task — Assesses prior belief updating when feedback about obtaining positive outcomes changes (prediction errors).
: Kamin Blocking Task — Examines the role of mismatches between learned priors and new information (prediction errors) in belief formation about event causes.
: Minnesota Trust Game — Assesses the degree to which people distinguish between their priors about others' motivations, such as selfishness and spite, and impersonal chance in one-shot trust game and dictator games.
: Dynamic Trust Game — Assesses degree to which people learn and update priors about trusting partners from dynamic social feedback (prediction error) in a social exchange game.

The therapy is designed to enhance local microcirculation and venous return. Patients will undergo VCT sessions 3 times per week for a duration of 4 weeks (12 sessions total), each lasting approximately 20 to 30 minutes, in addition to standard wound care.
: Standard Wound Care — To ensure consistency of treatment conditions, all participants will receive standardized wound management. Wounds will be cleansed using a standardized irrigation solution. A silver-containing hydrofiber dressing will be used as the primary dressing. For heavily exuding wounds, the silver hydrofiber dressing will be applied alone; for mildly to moderately exuding wounds, it will be combined with a cleansing gel. The same type of secondary dressing will be used consistently across all patients. This care is provided over a 4-week period.

## NCT07902284
Effects of Mirror Therapy and Motor Imagery on Upper Limb Motor Functions in Middle Cerebral Artery Stroke

Intervention: : Mirror Therapy — Participants sit with a mirror placed in the midsagittal plane, the affected limb hidden behind it and the unaffected limb reflected to create the illusion of normal movement. Therapist-guided training for 20 minutes per session (10 repetitions per task × 2 sets) progresses from simple shoulder, elbow, forearm and hand movements (Weeks 1-2), to reaching, grasp and release, and object manipulation (Weeks 3-4), to functional reaching, fine hand tasks, and speed and accuracy training (Weeks 5-6). It is combined with 30 minutes of routine Bobath-based physical therapy.
: Motor Imagery — Participants sit with eyes closed and mentally rehearse movements of the affected upper limb without physically performing them, using visual and kinesthetic imagery with standardized verbal cues. Sessions last 20 minutes (10 imagery trials per task × 2 sets) and progress from relaxation and imagery of simple movements (Weeks 1-2), to imagined reaching, grasp and release, and object manipulation (Weeks 3-4), to functional reaching, fine hand activities, ADL rehearsal and error correction (Weeks 5-6). It is combined with 30 minutes of routine Bobath-based physical therapy.
: Routine Physical Therapy — Routine physical therapy based on the Bobath concept, given to all participants for 30 minutes per session, 3 times per week for 6 weeks. It focuses on normalizing tone, facilitating normal movement patterns, weight shifting, postural control and functional upper limb activities while inhibiting abnormal movement patterns. Weeks 1-2: scapular mobilization, weight-bearing, trunk control, assisted ROM, sensory stimulation. Weeks 3-4: active-assisted reaching, elbow extension, wrist and hand opening, grasp and release. Weeks 5-6: task-oriented reaching, functional grasp, object manipulation, ADL-based practice. After 6 weeks, all participants follow a 6-week home exercise program.

## NCT07902297
Effects of Perturbation-Based Versus Conventional Balance Training on Reactive Stepping Ability in Patients With Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy

Intervention: : Perturbation-Based Balance Training (PBBT) — Participants will receive routine physical therapy (7 minutes of warm-up, 6 minutes of rest, and 7 minutes of cool-down) along with perturbation-based balance training for 8 weeks, with 3 supervised sessions per week (24 sessions, 60 minutes each). After a 2-week shared familiarization phase (weeks 1-2), participants will receive manually delivered, repeated exposure to unexpected and externally imposed postural perturbations by a physical therapist in standing position on stable and unstable surfaces (weeks 3-8). Perturbations will progress from anterior and posterior to multi-directional and randomized, and from standing tasks to walking, uneven surfaces, and dual-task conditions, increasing from 10 to 15 perturbations per session. A support bar and pre-session blood glucose monitoring will be used for safety.
: Conventional Balance Training (CBT) — Participants will receive routine physical therapy (7 minutes of warm-up, 6 minutes of rest, and 7 minutes of cool-down) along with conventional balance training for 8 weeks, with 3 supervised sessions per week (24 sessions, 60 minutes each). After a 2-week shared familiarization phase (weeks 1-2), participants will be trained for balance with eyes open and eyes closed in various conditions on stable and unstable surfaces, with no manual perturbations (weeks 3-8). Training will progress from foam-pad standing and weight shifting to functional gait tasks, obstacle negotiation, stair negotiation, and dual-task walking. A support bar and pre-session blood glucose monitoring will be used for safety.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07902297

Efficacy and Safety of Endovascular Thrombectomy With Versus Without Hypothermia in Acute Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: a Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : hypothermia — In this trial, intra-arterial selective cooling infusion is used to reduce brain tissue temperature. After thrombectomy, a microcatheter was advanced to the segment between the C6 segment of the internal carotid artery and the proximal M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery. To achieve rapid targeted cooling of the ischemic cerebral region, 0-4℃ of pre-cooled normal saline was infused through the microcatheter using precision infusion pumps. The brain temperature is monitored continuously at the sigmoid sinus as a surrogate marker. * Frequency: Median frequency (MDF) and mean frequency (MNF) calculated using the fast Fourier transform (FFT) with 0.5-1 s sliding windows.

Fatigue Indices

* Ratio of RMS at the end versus the beginning of the sustained contraction.
* Time to task failure (s) during sustained effort.

Quality Control:

## NCT07756606
Evaluating the Impacts of Informal Tick and Tickborne Disease Educational Tools on Children

Intervention: : Tick check mannequin — Nymphal and adult blacklegged ticks are glued to the mannequins to mimic potential acquisition or attachment sites. At outreach events, participants are invited to perform a thorough tick check on the mannequin. This activity helps participants identify the different life stages of the blacklegged tick and understand the size differences between nymphal and adult ticks. The "tick check" mannequins also wear both light and dark-colored clothing to show how clothing color affects tick detection.
: Ticks on bagel — Adult and nymphal blacklegged ticks are glued to an "everything" bagel. The bagel is covered in sesame and poppy seeds, which is the comparison commonly used to describe the size of adult and nymphal blacklegged ticks, respectively. Participants are then invited to search the bagel for ticks. The activity demonstrates the size differences between the adult and nymphal life stages and the proper search image for finding nymphs during a tick check.
: LEGO Build-a-Tick — The LEGO tick is an activity that leverages play-based learning to increase awareness of ticks and tick-borne diseases, and it has the potential to significantly enhance our educational efforts by increasing engagement. This Build-a-Tick Kit is comprised of 83 LEGO bricks and offers a hands-on learning experience with multiple learning outcomes. Participants learn about the various morphological parts of a blacklegged tick during the building experience, such as the mouth parts and their function in disease transmission, the number of legs, and the body shapes and colors for an adult blacklegged tick. Additional information on ticks and tick-borne diseases is incorporated into the building instructions included in the Build-a-Tick Kit.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07756606

SUMMARY:

## NCT07763431
Efficacy of Home-Use Dual-Light Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy as an Adjunct to Supportive Peri-Implant Care in Patients With Peri-Implant Mucositis Around Screw-Retained Full-Arch Implant-Supported Prostheses: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Dual-light antibacterial photodynamic therapy — An intraoral light-emitting device with 48 LEDs delivering 405 nm antibacterial blue light and 810 nm near-infrared light simultaneously in a 50:50 ratio, providing uniform illumination of both arches. Used with an indocyanine green photosensitizer rinse (250 µg/mL). Each session lasts 10 minutes at 30 J/cm2. Self-administered at home: once daily in weeks 1-2, twice daily in weeks 3-4.
: Supportive peri-implant care — Standardized supportive peri-implant care delivered according to the 2023 EFP S3-level clinical practice guideline for the prevention and treatment of peri-implant diseases, following an etiology-based, non-surgical approach: (1) assessment and control of risk factors, including smoking, glycemic control, and oral hygiene, with counselling; (2) evaluation of the fixed prosthesis and, where the design impairs access, removal of the screw-retained prosthesis to allow direct access to the implant necks and peri-implant soft tissue; (3) individualized oral hygiene instruction adapted to a full-arch fixed implant-supported prosthesis; (4) professional mechanical plaque removal above and below the mucosal margin using implant-safe plastic ultrasonic tips, without altering the implant surface; and (5) reassessment and reinforcement of oral hygiene at follow-up. No adjunctive antibiotics or antiseptics are used as part of the standard care.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07763431

## NCT07902518
The Use of Theta-Burst Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in the Treatment of Persistent Auditory Hallucinations: A Pilot Study

Intervention: : Theta-Burst Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TBS) — Theta-burst stimulation (TBS) will be delivered using a MagPro transcranial magnetic stimulation system (MagVenture) equipped with a B-70 coil.

Each session will combine bilateral continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS) targeting the temporoparietal junctions (900 pulses per hemisphere at 90% of the resting motor threshold) and intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (600 pulses at 120% of the resting motor threshold).

Stimulation targets will be identified using the international 10-20 EEG system (F3 for the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and the midpoint between T3 and P3 for the left temporoparietal junction).

Participants will receive two sessions daily over 10 weekdays, for a total of 20 treatment sessions.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07902518

Recovery Time With the Application of ALDRETE Score in Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Endoscopy: a Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : The post-anesthesia recovery or Aldrete score has been commonly used to clinically assess the physical status of patients recovering from the anesthetic experience and to follow their awakening proces — Patients randomized to the intervention arm upon arrival in the recovery area were assessed by endoscopy nurses experienced in Aldrete score implementation when discharging patients. The Aldrete score was calculated every 10 minutes using a structured questionnaire (Supplementary File B) and after a minimum of 10 minutes, patients could be discharged from the recovery area if their Aldrete score was ≥9, with their accompanying person. Patients assigned to the standard of care Group (SOC) were assessed in the recovery area by other endoscopy nurses in a subjective empirical manner. After a minimum of 10 minutes first, patients' vital signs and consciousness were assessed and if deemed within normal range the patient could be discharged also accompanied by the responsible person. In case the endoscopy nurse considered those requirements inadequate the patient remained in the recovery area and was re-evaluated 5 min later again assessing the same parameters. ## NCT07903675
Effectiveness of the Autism Pupil Screen (APS) Detect Pupillometer for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in Routine Healthcare

Intervention: : Autism Pupil Screen (APS) Detect PLR Assessment #1 — The APS Detect™ is an investigational handheld pupillometer that measures pupillary light reflex (PLR) responses using a brief, noninvasive assessment. Measurements obtained by the device are used to generate an Autism Pupil Screening (APS) score that is intended to help identify children who may be at risk for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) during routine pediatric healthcare visits. The APS Detect is investigational and has not been cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for clinical use.
: Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, Revised with Follow-up (M-CHAT/R-F) — A validated parent- or caregiver-completed screening tool used to identify children who may be at risk for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The questionnaire is designed for children between 16 and 30 months of age and consists of an initial screening questionnaire followed by a structured follow-up interview for children with positive screening results. The M-CHAT-R/F is intended to identify children who may benefit from further developmental and diagnostic evaluation for ASD.
: Social Responsiveness Scale, Second Edition (SRS-2) — A standardized questionnaire used to measure the presence and severity of social communication difficulties and restricted or repetitive behaviors associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The SRS-2 is completed by a parent, caregiver, teacher, or other knowledgeable respondent and provides quantitative scores that help assess social functioning and identify characteristics associated with ASD across a range of ages. It is intended to support the screening and evaluation of individuals who may have ASD and to monitor changes in social responsiveness over time.
: Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Second Edition (ADOS-2) — A standardized, play-based assessment administered by a trained clinician to evaluate social communication, social interaction, play, and restricted or repetitive behaviors associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The ADOS-2 consists of age- and language-specific assessment modules and is widely used as part of a comprehensive diagnostic evaluation to support the identification and classification of ASD.
: Mullen Scales of Early Learning (MSEL) — A standardized developmental assessment administered by a trained examiner to evaluate cognitive and developmental functioning in young children from birth through 68 months of age. The assessment measures visual reception, fine motor skills, receptive language, and expressive language and provides information about a child's developmental abilities relative to age-based expectations.
: Adaptive Behavior Assessment System, Third Edition (ABAS-3) — A standardized assessment completed by a parent, caregiver, teacher, or other knowledgeable respondent to evaluate adaptive functioning in everyday life. The ABAS-3 measures skills across conceptual, social, and practical domains, including communication, self-care, social interaction, community use, and functional academics. Results provide an assessment of an individual's ability to perform age-appropriate daily activities and support the evaluation of developmental, intellectual, and behavioral functioning.
: Autism Pupil Screen (APS) Detect PLR Assessment #2 — The APS Detect™ is an investigational handheld pupillometer that measures pupillary light reflex (PLR) responses using a brief, noninvasive assessment. Measurements obtained by the device are used to generate an Autism Pupil Screening (APS) score that is intended to help identify children who may be at risk for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) during routine pediatric healthcare visits. The APS Detect is investigational and has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for clinical use.

This intervention will be used for the second assessment with the APS Detect™ in Arm B, the precision sub-study to evaluate the reliability and reproducibility of the Autism Pupil Screening (APS) Detect™ investigational device.
: Autism Pupil Screen (APS) Detect Assessment #3 — The APS Detect™ is an investigational handheld pupillometer that measures pupillary light reflex (PLR) responses using a brief, noninvasive assessment. Measurements obtained by the device are used to generate an Autism Pupil Screening (APS) score that is intended to help identify children who may be at risk for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) during routine pediatric healthcare visits. The APS Detect is investigational and has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for clinical use.

This intervention will be used for the third assessment with the APS Detect™ in Arm B, the precision sub-study to evaluate the reliability and reproducibility of the Autism Pupil Screening (APS) Detect™ investigational device.
: Well-child check — A routine pediatric healthcare visit that includes assessment of growth, development, general health, and age-appropriate preventive care. The visit may include a physical examination, developmental surveillance, review of medical history, and discussion of health concerns with the child's parent or caregiver following the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) Bright Futures guidelines.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07903675

## NCT07904065
Comparison of Two Anorganic Xenografts in the Lateral Window Maxillary Sinus Augmentation Technique With or Without Mandibular Bone Marrow Blood Admixture: Histomorphometric, Radiographic and Clinical Analysis

Intervention: : Deproteinized Bovine Bone Mineral (Bio-Oss) — Deproteinized bovine bone mineral, large particle size (1-2 mm granules), manufactured by Geistlich Pharma AG (Wolhusen, Switzerland). Approximately 1-1.5 g is placed in the maxillary sinus after elevation of the Schneiderian membrane through a lateral window prepared with piezoelectric surgery. Used alone or mixed with mandibular marrow blood depending on the assigned arm. Reference (control) graft material.
: Deproteinized Bovine Bone Mineral (InterOss) — Deproteinized bovine bone mineral, large particle size (1-2 mm granules), manufactured by SigmaGraft Biomaterials (Fullerton, CA, USA). Approximately 1-1.5 g is placed in the maxillary sinus after elevation of the Schneiderian membrane through a lateral window prepared with piezoelectric surgery. Used alone or mixed with mandibular marrow blood depending on the assigned arm. Test graft material with physicochemical characteristics similar to Bio-Oss.
: Mandibular Bone Marrow Blood Aspiration — Autologous bone marrow blood harvesting following a modified University of Michigan protocol. Through a small full-thickness flap in the retromolar/external oblique ridge area, the mandibular cortex is perforated 4-5 mm deep with a round carbide bur to reach the medullary space. Approximately 0.5 mL of marrow blood is aspirated with a heparinized 21G catheter and syringe, collected in a heparinized container, and mixed with the bovine bone graft immediately before placement in the sinus. No cell processing or culture is performed.

## NCT07904299
Effect of an Intergenerational Interaction Program Between Older Adults Living in a Nursing Home and Nursing Students on Loneliness, Joy of Life, and Ageism: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Intergenerational Interaction Program — A 6-week intergenerational interaction program in which each older adult living in a nursing home is paired one-to-one with a nursing student. Pairs meet once a week for about 2 hours (1 introductory week + 5 activity weeks). Each session includes welcome and conversation (15 min), joint activity selection (5-10 min), a main activity (60-70 min), and mutual reflection and closing (20-25 min). Activities are chosen jointly by each pair from four categories: games and problem solving, reading and cultural sharing, creative work, and sharing skills and experiences. The program is structured around Allport's contact conditions: equal status, common goals, cooperation, institutional support, sustained contact, and reciprocity. Before the first visit, students receive brief training on aging, communication, and interacting with individuals with cognitive impairment, and they follow defined role boundaries (e.g., no medical or personal care).
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07904299

## NCT07904741
The Effect of Different Exercise Training Programs on Muscle Oxygenation, Strength, Pain, and Functionality in Individuals With Knee Osteoarthritis

Intervention: : Recumbent-Cycle Aerobic Exercise — Supervised aerobic exercise on a recumbent cycle ergometer, three times per week for 6 weeks (18 sessions). Each session includes a 5-minute warm-up and a 5-minute cool-down. At the beginning of the program, the main cycling will be at 40% to 50% of age-predicted maximum heart rate. Duration and intensity are progressed according to participant tolerance, with a target at 60% to 70% of maximum heart rate by week 6. Cadence is 60 to 80 revolutions per minute. Heart rate and perceived exertion are monitored during exercise.
: Lower-Limb Strengthening Exercise — Supervised bilateral lower-limb strengthening exercise, three times per week for 6 weeks (18 sessions). Exercises include isometric knee extension, hip flexion, extension, abduction and adduction, clamshell exercise, and knee flexion and extension using ankle weights. Participants perform 1 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions, with 90 to 120 seconds of rest between sets. Resistance starts at approximately 30% of one-repetition maximum and may progress toward 60%, according to tolerance and pain response. One-repetition maximum is reassessed every 2 weeks.
: Home Flexibility Exercise Program — Home flexibility exercises provided to participants in all three arms. The program includes bilateral standing hamstring and quadriceps stretches and a towel-assisted gastrocnemius stretch. Each stretch is held at the point of tension for 20 to 30 seconds. Participants are asked to perform the exercises 3 to 5 days per week.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07904741

SUMMARY:

Selection of acupuncture points has been based on the recommendation of traditional Chinese medicine.
: Warmth only — A custom-built warmth pad surrounding the TENS electrodes could produce the controlled comfortable warmth sensation, with default setting at 37degrees to 40 degrees Celsius. No built-in TENS electrodes in the cap.

## NCT03713268
Intraoperative OCT Guidance of Intraocular Surger

Intervention: : Microscope integrated optical coherence tomography — This is translational study in which subjects will either be imaged with a microscope integrated optical coherence tomography (MIOCT) system or they will use MIOCT during surgical procedures. OCT systems are optical imaging technology that allow non-contact imaging of the microanatomy of the retina, cornea, optic nerve head and retinal blood vessels. The MIOCT has been integrated into the surgical microscope used in retinal and anterior segment surgeries so it does not touch the eye. Unlike visible light from many examination devices, the infrared OCT beam is barely visible to the human eye as it sweeps across the retina. Thus the patient is not disturbed by the light.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03713268

: Diphenhydramine — Preparative/Conditioning Regime r-ATG premedication according to institutional guidelines

A Multicentre, Prospective, Randomized, Multi-arm, Multi-stage Clinical Trial of High-flow Oxygen for Vaso-occlusive Pain Crisis in Adult Patients With Sickle Cell Disease;

Intervention: : Stadard low-flow oxygen — In the control group, standard low-flow oxygen will be delivered via nasal prongs (LFNO), up to hospital discharge or secondary ACS onset, in order to achieve normoxia (target pulse oxymetry saturation of 95%). This strategy is in accordance with current recommendations and usual care

Intervention: : maCBT — Multimodal Antecedent-focussed Cognitive-behavioural Training (maCBT) is an individual manualized psychological intervention. It follows an integrated model focussed on normalisation of the unusual experiences, their re-appraisal, exploring helpfulness of current coping, and developing a repertoire of strategies to decrease the impact of these experiences on the young person's life. The maCBT follows a manual describing obligatory and optional therapeutic elements, proposed list of modules, outline of a therapeutic session, and the integrated cognitive model. The intervention will be delivered in 8 to 16 one-hour sessions in an individual format. Sessions will be initially weekly, and then spaced out to once every two weeks in the latter stages of the intervention.

## NCT04363983
Interaction Between Host, Microenvironment and Immunity on Gastrointestinal Neoplasms: A Retro-prospective Cohort Study

Intervention: : Blood sampling — Blood collection (50 ml) will be performed for all patients at baseline, at 1 month post-operative for resected patients (+ at the end of neoadjuvant treatment / before surgery if patient receives neoadjuvant treatment), and at 2-3 months after the beginning of the treatments in patients with metastases (+ at each progression).

Following analysis should be performed with

* serum for protein assays and characterization analysis of cytokines, new tumor markers and micro-RNA ...;
* plasma for protein assays and characterization analysis of micro-RNA, VEC (the content of proteins, RNA, micro-RNA and DNA) and metabolomics;
* PBMC for flow cytometry analysis, isolation macrophages;
* whole blood for circulating tumor DNA (mutations by NGS, ddPCR,…; methylation) and circulating tumor cells.
: Liver biopsy — An intraoperative liver biopsy will be performed at free edge of liver with a triangular sample for local resected patients.

This biopsy will be done with scissors, then patients will receive intraoperative hemostasis with mono- or bipolar coagulation. This procedure will be under laparoscopy or laparotomy without extending standard processing time.

This biopsy seeks to allow the evaluate liver modifications testifying the preparing for premetastatic niche, which would allow to identify the patients with risk for hepatic relapsing; the same analysis on the tumors will be performed.
: Stool collect — Stool collection will be performed for all patients at baseline, at 1 month post-operative for resected patients (+ at the end of neoadjuvant treatment / before surgery if patient receives neoadjuvant treatment), and at 2-3 months after the beginning of the treatments in patients with metastases (+ at each progression).

Analysis will be performed for microbiota and metabolism analysis.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04363983

## NCT07593222
Synaptic Mechanisms of Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation for Major Depressive Disorder

Intervention: : Sham iTBS — ham intermittent theta burst stimulation delivered to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex using a sham coil identical in appearance to the active coil. No active magnetic stimulation is delivered. Used to control for the sensory experience of TMS.
: TMS — Active intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) delivered to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex combined with oral placebo. iTBS consists of 50 Hz triplets delivered in 2-second bursts at 5 Hz, totaling 600 pulses per session over approximately 3 minutes, delivered using a figure-of-8 coil with real-time neuronavigation at an intensity set relative to each participant's resting motor threshold.
: D-cycloserine — D-cycloserine at 100 mg acts as a partial agonist at the glycine co-agonist site of the NMDA receptor, facilitating NMDAR-mediated synaptic transmission. It is administered orally approximately 2 hours before iTBS to coincide with near-peak plasma concentration. Compounded as 100 mg capsules.
: Dextromethophan — Dextromethorphan at 150 mg acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist, blocking NMDAR-mediated synaptic transmission at brain concentrations consistent with in vitro receptor blockade. Administered orally approximately 2 hours before iTBS.
: Placebo — Microcrystalline cellulose capsule identical to the drug capsules, administered 2 hours prior to iTBS treatment.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07593222

## NCT07712783
Comparison of the Analgesic Efficacy of Lateral Quadratus Lumborum Block and Intrathecal Morphine for Postoperative Pain Management Following Cesarean Delivery Under Spinal Anesthesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Lateral Quadratus Lumborum Block — Active Lateral QLB Local anesthetic: 0.25% bupivacaine, 0.4 mL/kg perside (maximum 30 mL per side). Maximum total dose: Bupivacaine ≤2.5 mg/kg (maximum approximately 150 mg). Timing: Immediately after completion of surgery. The patient will be positioned supine or in a slight lateral decubitus position. A high-frequency linear US transducer (5-12 MHz) will be placed on the anterolateral abdominal wall at the T12-L1 level. The fascial plane will be identified under ultrasound guidance. A 22-gauge, 100-mm needle will be advanced using an in-plane approach, and after negative aspiration, the local anesthetic will be injected incrementally with hydrodissection confirming correct spread.

Sham ITM: The spinal anesthesia technique will be identical to that of the active ITM group. Morphine will be replaced with 0.2 mL preservative-free normal saline, while maintaining an identical syringe volume (2.7 mL) and appearance.
: ıv morphine PCA — A standardized IV PCA protocol will be initiated for all patients using a PCA device (Body Guard 575 pain manager, UK), programmed to deliver morphine boluses of 0.01-0.015 mg/kg (IBW), with a 6-minute lockout and a 4-hour maximum dose of 0.1-0.15 mg/ kg (IBW). No basal infusion will be used.
: Intrathecal morphine — Hyperbaric 0.5% bupivacaine 12.5 mg, fentanyl 20 µg, and morphine 80 µg (0.08 mg). Spinal anesthesia will be performed at the L3-L4 or L4-L5 intervertebral space using a 25-gauge Quincke spinal needle. The study solution will be prepared to a total volume of 2.7 mL.

Sham QLB Following completion of surgery, the patient will be positioned in the lateral decubitus position. The ultrasound transducer will be placed over the lateral QLB scanning window. A 22-gauge needle will be advanced into the skin and subcutaneous tissue only, without entering the fascial plane. To maintain procedural standardization and preserve blinding, 1-2 mL of normal saline will be injected into the subcutaneous tissue. Procedure duration, patient positioning, ultrasound probe placement, and dressing application will be identical to those used for the active lateral QLB-I procedure. A sterile dressing will be applied at the end of the procedure.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07712783

## NCT07785102
SPARC-LI: Synaptic Plasticity Augmented Rapid Circuit Stimulation

Intervention: : TMS — Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS): TMS involves a procedure where a coil is placed on the scalp and magnetic energy enters the participant's brain in pulses. TMS does not alter consciousness or impose restrictions of any kind on a participant after a session. Single pulses of TMS are delivered to probe cortical excitability, as a surrogate of plasticity, before and after each treatment session. Excitability is measured with neurophysiology including electromyography (EMG). Repetitive TMS (rTMS) administered in the study is delivered in a pattern protocol called intermittent-theta burst stimulation (iTBS) which has been FDA-cleared for-and shown to be effective in-the treatment of depression. We aim to deliver up to 20 sessions per day but can adapt for patient or staff related scheduling challenges or tolerability

## NCT07906288
Effectiveness of Clown Therapy in Facilitating Dental Visits for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder

Intervention: : Familiarization sessions using clown therapy — The familiarization activities will be conducted by two dentists and medical clowns.

T1 ( Session 1): The session will be conducted exclusively by the medical clowns, who will perform a brief educational and playful show aimed at explaining the steps of a dental visit in an engaging manner, using toys. Interaction with the clowns through games and sketches will be encouraged. No direct intervention by the dentist or active involvement of the child will occur during this session.

T2 (Session 2): The session will involve interaction among the patient, the clown therapists, and the parent. The parent will be gradually engaged, while the dentist's intervention will be directed primarily toward thoward the clown therapists and/or the parent, maintaining an indirect approach toward the child.

T3 (Session 3): The session will include interaction with the medical clowns, intervention by the dentist directed toward the clowns and the parent, and finally direct involvement of the child.
: Familiarization sessions with conventional methods — Patients will participate in three consecutive sessions (T1, T2, and T3), scheduled at weekly intervals. The familiarization activities will be conducted exclusively by two dentists, in the presence of at least one parent or legal guardian.

T1 (Session 1): Introduction to the dental operatory and dental chair using basic behavioral management techniques, including tell-show-do and desensitization. The instruments required for a dental examination (mouth mirror and dental explorer) will also be introduced.

T2 (Session 2): Repetition of the activities performed during T1, with a simulated dental examination carried out on the parent (modeling technique) to encourage patient cooperation.

T3 (Session 3): Following a brief review of the activities completed during T1 and T2, the patient will be invited to sit in the dental chair and undergo a clinical examination according to standard assessment procedures.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07906288

SUMMARY:

## NCT07906821
Ultrasound-guided Microwave Ablation of Benign Thyroid Nodules

Intervention: : ultrasound-guided percutaneous microwave ablation (MWA) — Under ultrasound guidance, the microwave electrode was inserted targeted to the nodule. Ablation is carried out one axial plane at a time, from inferior to superior aspect of the targeted lesion. Within each axial plane, ablation is performed from deep to superficial manner to prevent bubble generated by the ablation from hindering ultrasound examination. The extent of the ablated zone is determined real-time by the echogenic changes around the electrode. Ablation will be away from important structure, including major vessels, recurrent laryngeal nerve and trachea. During the procedure, the patient's vital signs including O2 saturation, blood pressure and heart rate would be monitored. Operative procedures, difficulties encountered (if any) and operation time will be documented.

Intervention: : Nutricional Education and General Exercise Guidelines — Participants will receive standardized nutritional education and general physical exercise guidelines through a structured information booklet. An initial face-to-face session will be conducted to explain the educational materials and recommendations. A second face-to-face follow-up session will be held midway through the 12-week intervention period to answer questions, reinforce the recommendations, and review adherence to the proposed nutritional and exercise guidelines. No structured strength training or supervised exercise sessions will be provided as part of this intervention.
: Progressive Resistance Training With Cognitive Dual-Task Training — Participants will receive standardized nutritional education and complete a 12-week supervised progressive resistance training program combined with cognitive dual-task training. Training will be performed twice weekly and will target the lower limbs, upper limbs, and trunk using dumbbells, resistance bands, weights, and bodyweight exercises. Training intensity will be individually adjusted and progressively increased toward 60%-90% of one-repetition maximum (1-RM). Training load will be periodically adjusted according to participant progression. Cognitive tasks will be performed simultaneously with physical exercises to address cognitive-motor interference.
: Progressive Resistance Training With Cognitive Dual-Task and Inestability Training — Participants will receive standardized nutritional education and complete a 12-week supervised progressive resistance training program combined with cognitive dual-task training and instability components. Training will be performed twice weekly and will target the lower limbs, upper limbs, and trunk. The same relative strength-training intensity and load principles as the PRT intervention will be applied. Additional instability and postural control demands will be incorporated through unstable surfaces and other postural challenges. Training intensity and complexity will be individually adapted according to functional and cognitive status.
